items.title: Expecting mother threatens to cut off her sister if she doesn't come to her gender reveal party when she has pneumonia: 'I also have a child who she’s never met.'
items.text:
You would think that a woman who is carrying her child wouldn't want to be around somebody who has a serious illness, but I guess she cares more about the party than she cares about the baby's safety.

I love to host parties. Every couple of months, my roommates and I invite our 200 closest friends to our apartment for a themed house party, and at least 60 of them show up without fail. We have developed a reputation for hosting pretty fun parties. Zack, my roommate who is great in the kitchen, makes a huge vat of special-flavored punch for all the guests, so we never run out of what keeps the party going. My other roommate, Audrey, loves to transform our space, and she makes incredible decorations that really set our house parties apart from others. I invite the majority of the party guests, mostly members of my adult recreational sports league. When we work together, we can create something wonderful. I am grateful to have roommates who are not only comfortable with us hosting parties, but also willing to put in the work to make them great.

Over the years, I've learned you really can't be too sensitive about people bailing on your events, especially house parties. Even though I know one person not showing up won't totally change the event's trajectory, it still sometimes hurts my feelings. The worst part of the party planning experience is an hour or two before it starts, when people start sending you paragraph-long texts about why they can't make it. I know not everyone would agree, but I would rather party guests not show up than try to justify bailing. I would understand a long text explaining why you're bailing on an intimate dinner, but for a big party, I don't think it's a crime to just bail without explaining yourself. The worst is when people go from RSVPing "Going" to RSVPing "Maybe" on the day of the party. At that point, just RSVP "Can't Go," and move along!

Even though I am a little sensitive when people bail on my parties, I know my party isn't the most important thing happening in their life right now. If someone is sick or not feeling up to it, I would never judge them for skipping. I know a 27th birthday party isn't that big a deal, so I won't judge my friends for putting themselves first.

Some events in life you really want your friends and family to be there for. If my best friend missed my baby shower or my wedding because she had a slight cold, I would be pretty upset. But if she had a serious, spreadable illness that she had not recovered from, I would not want her to take the risk of coming to an event with a ton of people. The sister in this story cares more about her party than her sister's health, her own, or her guests', and that is sad to behold.

items.title: Introverted Cat Memes That Make Staying Home This Weekend Sound Purrfect
items.text:
Some cats are social butterflies, and others would rather hide under the bed until everyone leaves. They have no interest in making new friends, attending family gatherings, or entertaining unexpected visitors. If they could put a "Do Not Disturb" sign on their favorite hiding spot, we're pretty sure they would.

Can we blame them? As fellow introverts know, socializing can be exhausting. Sometimes you just want to spend the evening curled up somewhere comfortable, enjoying your own company without anyone asking you questions. Cats have been living that dream for centuries, and they don't even have to come up with excuses to cancel plans.

We think introverted cats might actually have the right idea. Why bother making small talk when you could be taking your fourth nap of the afternoon? Why entertain guests when there's a purrfectly good cardboard box waiting in the bedroom? And why leave the house when everything you need is already there, including a hooman servant who delivers meals?

Some kitties take their antisocial tendencies to impressive lengths. The doorbell rings, and they're gone before you've even gotten off the couch. A friend comes over, and suddenly your cat has vanished into another dimension. You'll spend the entire visit explaining that yes, you really do own a cat, and no, you have absolutely no idea where they're hiding.

Then, the second everyone leaves, your little hermit comes strolling out like nothing happened. They'll stretch, demand dinner, and look mildly annoyed that you've disturbed their peaceful afternoon. Once the coast is finally clear, normal feline business can resume.

We also love how introverted cats can be incredibly affectionate with their chosen humans while wanting absolutely nothing to do with anyone else. They'll happily spend hours curled up beside you, but introduce one unfamiliar person and suddenly they're unavailable for the foreseeable future. Their social circle is small, their standards are high, and they're not accepting applications.

We'd love to borrow some of that confidence. Imagine being able to disappear from an awkward conversation without explaining yourself, or simply walking away when you've had enough. Cats don't worry about seeming rude. They've got important purrsonal business to attend to, and that usually involves sleeping.

So if your ideal weekend involves staying home, avoiding crowds, and enjoying a little peace and quiet, these introverted cat memes should feel awfully familiar. Grab your favorite blanket, silence those notifications, and enjoy some quality me-time with the internet's most relatable little homebodies.

items.title: Bride’s Father Leaves Wedding Immediately After Walking His Daughter Down the Aisle: ‘He walked over to my in-laws and said he was “feeling sick” so he left’
items.text:
Some parents can't handle not being the centre of attention, but you can't point it out to them because they won't admit it

Your wedding is supposed to be your night. It's one of those (rare) occasions in which the spotlight is on you. Yet some parents still manage to make it about themselves.

They might genuinely feel that they're getting sick, or have intense stomach pain out of the blue, and have to storm out of the party, leaving everyone worried.

Imagine you're so committed to making everything about yourself that you do it unconsciously. I guess you can't blame them, because if they do it unconsciously, they're not doing it on purpose. You can and should get mad at them, though, because they can ruin your night, but in the end, it's because they likely have a very deep psychological wound. Otherwise, why would you do that?

Seeing somebody else shine might trigger feelings of inadequacy for them. They don't consciously want to sabotage your happiness, but they can't tolerate the feelings that arise when somebody else is the center of attention.

Of course, you can't discuss something they aren't even aware of, so you're likely stuck having to process it on your own. If they were aware of this, they would probably manage it in another way, by talking to you or somebody they trust, and trying to resolve their issues. But they can't, and it manifests as sudden stomach aches or itching. If it really is like this, there is nothing you can do about it.

I was the first in my family to go to college, and when I finally got in, I remember my father looked at me in the eye and said I should go back to school because I was surpassing him. He looked very worried. Instead of being proud, he took it upon himself and saw his own daughter as competence.

Luckily, at that time, I only saw him as a wounded person, and I didn't think too much of it, but he did stuff like that many times years later, and I think it all had to do with his own frustrations.

Anyways, having unresolved psychological issues might explain why you behave in a certain way, but it doesn't excuse you. You still have responsibility for your actions.

That's the most frustrating thing about dealing with people like this: you can understand where their actions come from, but that doesn't mean you should silently accept everything they do. And it certainly doesn't make their behaviour any less hurtful.

When you're dealing with emotionally immature people, you'll end up comforting them for something they did to you, and that's simply not fair. That's why you should be very careful with who you choose to spend your time with, and it doesn't matter if it's family or not.

Understanding someone psychologically doesn't mean you can stop them from ruining your party.

What you can do is uninvite them from the next one! Cheers.

items.title: 17 Common Money Mistakes That May Jeopardize Your Finances
items.text:
Sometimes you make a decision that you don't realize will have a ripple effect throughout the rest of your life.

I, for one, don't always make decisions thinking in the long term. Sometimes I'm all about the short term. I'm trying to get through today, and I'm not always thinking about tomorrow. This isn't a great way to live. It's good to live in the moment, but it's also essential to plan for your future. It can be overwhelming to think about, but it's necessary sometimes. Especially when it comes to money. Money famously doesn't grow on trees, and it can take a while to build up a base for yourself. It can take time, and a little bit of acumen. But it's hard to sift through all of the advice that's out there. There is so much of it out there that it's easy to get lost in the sauce. That's why it's nice to hear from real people every now and again.

items.title: Aunt demands 15-year-old babysit 7 kids at Halloween party, mom considers sending her $15 hourly rate: 'What else is a teenager doing on a Saturday night?'
items.text:
Should childcare always be free just because a parent is related to the person providing it?

Finding a good babysitter is the ultimate challenge for any parent who still wants to have some form of a social life that doesn't always involve their kids. There is nothing wrong with wanting some time that is adults-only now and then, but this is something that is likely to come at a price. The person who is most likely to take on any childcare duties without complaint is the one who is getting a paycheck out of it.

Of course, most parents would argue that it isn't unreasonable to expect a family member to provide some free babysitting now and again. Most moms and dads hope that they have some kind of village to fall back on when they really need it.

However, there is a big difference between generous relatives offering their help on their own terms and expecting them to watch the kids at the drop of a hat. Even the most willing of babysitters is likely to get a little bitter if their childcare becomes something that doesn't even warrant a proper discussion. Although the topic of compensation can be controversial when a family member helps out with the kids, it is sometimes appropriate to bring it up. For younger babysitters in particular, this may be one of their few forms of income, and it makes it worth it to give up their free time in favor of caring duties.

items.title: Stray Kitten Rescued From a Vent Under a House Parkours Into a Car and Wedges Himself Inside the Dashboard, Has to Be Re-Rescued, and Sparks Hilarious Responses From Online Cat Community
items.text:
Were cats the original parkour content creators? We're starting to think so…

Have you heard of the thrilling craze of parkour? This is someone who basically ricochets off buildings and other human-made objects found in cities and towns. They bounce around like a ninja in the night. When someone is good at it, it's actually pretty crazy to watch. When someone is bad at it… Well, it's quite literally painful to watch.

However, it's an amazing spectacle for us humans because the moves you do when parkouring are not natural. They take a lot of training and practice. When a cat moves around as if they practice parkour, it's pretty normal to watch. That's because cats are agile and always land on their feet. It's not crazy to see them bouncing off of one wall, to balancing on a skinny banister, back to another wall, and into your lap like nothing even happened. That's why we say "cat-like reflexes," because they move even better than a parkour professional!

So when this recently rescued kitten decided to show off his parkour skills right after being rescued from a vent underneath a house, it was a surprise, but not a shock.

items.title: 22 Wholesome Cats for a Softer Day on the Internet (October 24, 2026)
items.text:
Could your day use a little extra softness?

Have you ever experience that feeling where you don't what to do with the internet? Nowadays, the World Wide Web is full of sad news, conflicts, political news… It's become a source of sadness. Even though it's okay to keep track of what's going on in the world, it can take a toll on us. Sometimes, we just want to get online, look for something cute or fun, and move on with the rest of the day. But it gets complicated when you're stuck with a bunch of news you never meant to see. Being mindful of what you see online takes effort, because it can really affect your mood.

I've been reading about this lately, and many users have confirmed they feel down whenever they go online. And honestly, I agree, since it's happened to me more than I would like. Staying in touch with internet culture and the latest trends takes a lot of time online, but I have one strategy that helps me stay grounded and focused before I get sucked into the bad-news spiral. And that's actually searching for any kind of animal content, whether it's a story about a man and his lion or some good, wholesome cat memes. It always works.

items.title: 'One More Chapter': 22 Book Memes Keeping Readers Up Way Past Bedtime
items.text:
When did it become easier to scroll for an hour than to read one more chapter?

These days, I sometimes reach for my phone before I've given a book a chance to pull me in. I used to read for entire afternoons! And even keep going well into the night. Why did I lose my powers? I used to be very good at ignoring the real world and diving into the fictional one. The problem is that there's always something else to look at, and giving our full attention is getting harder and harder as the stories we consume every day on our phones get shorter. We want the introduction, middle, and end all right now, and books take their time to build the characters and the story. So, of course, we have no patience. TikTok and Instagram Reels offer much more instant fun, so we fall into their traps. But books have another charm. I miss being able to give a story my full attention.

My mom made me fall in love with reading. When I was little, we would read together in bed. She read to me aloud, and I looked at the illustrations on the pages. Eventually, I began reading on my own. It was so easy to get invested in a story. Books became something I wanted around all the time.

If we went to the mall, I always wanted to go into a bookstore. I'd always find something I wanted and ask my mom to buy it for me. Getting into a saga made this a recurring situation. I had finished one book, which meant I now had a very reasonable explanation for needing another. I couldn't leave the characters halfway through their problems.

items.title: The Wall of Weird: Spooky Stories of People Seeing Strange Stuff That No One Else Believed
items.text:
What better time of the year to talk about all of our spooky stories than Spooky Week itself?

There's only a week left until Halloween, and our decorations are up, the party invitations are already sent (or received, if you're not hosting), and our costumes are hanging in our closets until it's time to put them on. The jack-o'-lanterns are carved, the candies to give to the kids trick-or-treating are already bought, and all that's left is to sit down and wait until the day finally comes. But what do we do in the meantime? After all, we're already filled with the spooky spirit, and we don't want it to get cold, so how do we keep the scary adrenaline in our systems until next Saturday? Well, there are a few options.

First, and an old-time favourite: horror movies! There are so many classics we can turn to to keep our scary moods up. No matter how many times we've seen them, we always fall for the jump scares. And if you're not a fan af true horror, that's no problem! We can scale down a little bit and choose something along the suspense lines. The Haunting of Bly Manor is a favourite of mine, and yes, it could be qualified as horror, but don't worry; what scares you is the anticipation; there is nothing too graphic. We can always turn to Disney's Halloween movies; they have quite a few and are really good.

Or, if you prefer, telling your own weird and spooky stories will keep us all interested. It doesn't even have to be scary; all things weird and unusual are welcome!

items.title: Man lets brother pay $3400 for beachside rental, tells parents he booked them a vacation for their 40th anniversary: 'The whole table was congratulating him'
items.text:
Why should somebody get to take the credit for a vacation that doesn't affect their bank balance?

Sibling rivalries sound like something that should get left behind in childhood, but that couldn't be further from the truth a lot of the time. In fact, it is not uncommon for unfortunate behaviors and difficult family relationships to only get worse as people get older. All family dynamics are complicated in some ways, but some are more complicated than others.

Being on the receiving end of a sibling who doesn't want to behave doesn't get any easier as we get older. If anything, it is even more annoying when dealing with an adult who should know better. What is even more infuriating is that they aren't necessarily going to learn their lesson if you take action against them. It is like fighting in the backseat of Mom's car all over again.

The unfortunate truth is that a lot of people feel more entitled to take liberties with others when they happen to be related to them. They figure that because they're family, they'll have their back even when they do wrong. Of course, this couldn't be further from the truth, but this leaves the target of their conniving in an uncomfortable position. Sometimes, it causes more drama than it's worth to call them out. At the same time, if an issue of money or respect is on the line, it can feel like it is important to make sure that they get taken down a peg.

items.title: ‘SpongeBob Foods I Wish I Could Try’: 13 Delicious Iconic Meals From Bikini Bottom We All Wanted to Try
items.text:
Do you remember the 'Krusty Krab Training Video'? I remember it so vividly it feels like I was the one trained

For every new Krusty Krab employee, the ultimate career goal is to create a mouth-watering Krabby Patty by hand. However, before one can even think of picking up a spatula, one must thoroughly learn the ropes of the restaurant game, and the Krusty Krab Training Video is the perfect tool for fine-tuning the fresh new cog enthusiastically entering the service industry machine.

Ever since I was a kid, I've been trying to find what the secret formula is for the Krabby Patties. Some might say I've become more and more like Sheldon J. Plankton as time went by. I've always been fascinated by how the food, or more specifically the Krabby Patties, looked so delicious in SpongeBob.

I can totally understand why Plankton was so obsessed with stealing the secret formula. I just wanna say I don't understand why they were so mean to him when they could've integrated him into the team, worked together, and made everyone happy, lol. Although if they had done that, the show would've had no reason to go on, so I do get it; I just don't morally agree with it. But morality toward the 'bad guys' in cartoons is a whole other conversation.

My personal favorite delicious iconic meal from SpongeBob was the "Pretty Patties", the Krabby Patties that initially came in six different colours in the episode "Patty Hype". They were created by SpongeBob in an attempt to attract more customers to the restaurant.

I simply thought coloured hamburgers were such a great idea and that I would've loved to try one in real life, even if they are full of food colouring. I guess you could also attempt a healthier version by colouring ingredients with natural dye; anything can be done if you put your mind to it- just make the coloured patties already!

When I was researching this, I came across this wonderful website I didn't know existed that is called Ecyclopaedia SpongeBobia, and I believe it's my duty as a SpongeBob fan to share it with the world.

Anyway, back to the Krusty Krab training video. In that episode, I learned that (to put it in Mr. Krabs' words) "The money is always right!", and that pretty much sums up why I find that character and the entire show's universe so funny.

Did you know Mr. Krabs built the Krusty Krab from an Old retirement home? This backstory gives him much more depth as a character and really adds to the Krusty Krab's history. At first glance, you might feel every character is ridiculous, but as you learn more about the show, you realize every detail makes sense.

items.title: Bridesmaid buys a $230 dress for sister-in-law's wedding, gets kicked out of the bridal party less than a month before the ceremony, then the bride has the audacity to demand she hand it over for free: ‘I bought that dress with MY money’
items.text:
What happens when a bride kicks you out of her wedding party but still expects you to hand over the $230 dress you paid for?

Is a wedding really without some bridal drama? I get it: we're all getting nervous as the big day approaches, and a bit of selfishness comes with the punches. What can we say? I've attended a lot of weddings, and I can always say there was some kind of drama, most of it about the bride and her bridesmaids. They either couldn't agree on a color, a shape, or how to line up for pictures. Needless to say, I know these stories well.

But what surprised me most was that the bride literally kicked out this bridesmaid less than a month before the wedding because her fiancé's sister wanted to be in. Why wasn't this discussed earlier? They could've avoided this whole problem if they'd talked about it before going dress shopping. The woman bought her own bridesmaid dress for a hefty $230, and it's not wrong for her to want the full amount back before donating it to the person taking her spot.

items.title: Woofy Goofy Puppy Photos for a Wholesome Dose of Weekend Laughter
items.text:
There is nothing that can not be improved if you add a wholesome splash of puppies to it!

Now that the cooler seasons are coming, I don't know about you guys, but I get the urge to find cozy, wholesome, and cuddly things to fill my heart with warmth and pawsitivity.

Finding a cozy blanket and sitting on the couch holding a warm puppy is my top autumn activity, that is, along with taking never-ending naps. Puppies are the epitome of cuteness, and they are so soft and fluffy that they can also work as the perfect pillow. Besides, they are so little and new to the world that they end up being the most clumsy and adorable little creatures. They are still learning to walk, to eat without making a mess, and to discover all the world and all the things there are to smell. Their little runs, their high-pitched barks, their short little paws that are so cute and small you could eat them up! There's nothing about them that isn't absolutely perfect, and their shenanigans are the funniest thing you will ever see.

items.title: Mother brings her friends to her daughter's house while she's away and, without asking permission; then gets upset when her daughter tells her she'll do the same: 'She doesn’t want a bunch of people she doesn’t know in her house'
items.text:
A mother had her daughter's security code for the entrance, and while her daughter was away for her cousin's wedding, she took all her friends into her daughter's house for a gathering without asking her first. The daughter found out through her security cameras and told her mother that she would bring her own friends into her house on a random day.

What is it with parents and their nearly total lack of boundaries toward their children's private property?

It's baffling to me that some parents seem to think that they still have the right to enter their children's homes without asking first. It's not like they're teenagers locking themselves in their rooms while still living in mom and dad's house. Even then, the kids should have a right ot their privacy, but even more so when they actually move out.

The weird thing about growing up in a normal family, with healthy parents, is that you end up comparing yourself to all the crazy family stories you hear everywhere, and end up getting all outraged when you hear how little boundaries exist out there, and how little respect parents tend to have for their own children.

I know for a fact that my mother would never get into my house while I'm away without telling me, much less would she bring strange people into my place without my knowledge. Unlike my own, this mother didn't have that kind of consideration towards her daughter and her home.

items.title: A Happy Bag of Memes That Make You Feel Like Everything is Going to Be Okay
items.text:
Do you smell that? Is that?… Is that hope?! Fall brings more than just crisp morning, it also brings new beginnings and a time to embrace rest.

The harvest full moon is upon us. That means we are fully in fall mode! We harvest, we stock up for the cold months, and then we rest. This is the time of year when it is totally socially acceptable to stay inside and not go out. Go ahead and flake on those plans! But not until after Halloween. I mean, you do you, but Halloween is the best part of the year. Better than New Year's or St. Patrick's Day. This is when you can get all of your partying out of your system before you get comfy cozy at home wrapped in 1,000 blankets. It's a time for happiness! Sure, contemplate under some grey skies all you want, but find that balance. You need to find your happy place within the cold. It's not always easy to find the light in the dark tunnel after several months of winter, so get all that happiness you can right now during fall! You can start with these ultra-positive, happy, feel-good memes!

items.title: A Box of 23 Cardboard-Loving Cat Memes That Fit & Sit in Your Heart
items.text:
Cats never miss an opportunity to jump into every space, no matter its size or availability status.

I don't need to iterate on how cats enter every cardboard box they see, or literally any other small space they locate. But first - why do they even do that? In short, cats simply feel safe inside. Having an enclosed space around them, like a cardboard box, gives them a sense of security - however real or not. They also view these spaces as strategic vantage points to pounce on prey from - so basically a place to cosplay big cats. So basically it's just another proof that cats make no sense at all. Their logic is not logicing. But this is why we love them so much.

My cat found herself in the most ridiculous situations because of this internal drive she has to enter literally anywhere. To do the fits and sits even if she doesn't fit and cannot sit. She once got herself stuck behind the washing machine because she absolutely insisted this nook must be explored - she just had no idea how to get herself out. At another time, she got locked inside the pots and pans cabinet, which is protected by a child lock. It was open for one second, and she still managed to get herself inside.

But all of that doesn't make her experience with classic cardboard boxes any easier. That child lock I've mentioned? It's there for a reason. The reason being a 1-year-old roaming free in the house because she's been walking since she was 10 months old. That kid sees the cat entering a cardboard box I left on the floor for her and thinks, "I'm going to get inside to cuddle the cat." My cat bolts away every single time. Raising cats and kids together is not a simple task.

But cats will always cat, and that means they'll fit, sit, and be absolutely smug about it. And honestly? It makes them even more special than they already are.

items.title: Update: 20-year-old Airbnb guest in Nevada faces $58k in damages after shower handle comes off at 2 AM and floods the rental—returns 9 months later with an update: 'I know I didn’t directly cause the damage'
items.text:
While staying at an Airbnb in Nevada, a shower malfunctioned around 2 a.m., spraying water and causing damage. The host blamed the guest and requested $58,000 in damages. The guest returns now, nine months later, to provide an update on what has happened since.

When are guests responsible for accidental damage to a short-term rental? And when is that just a cost of doing business?

items.title: Strict vegan adopts very first kitten, then realizes that her tiny carnivore needs meat for life, and cat owners have a tough message for her: 'Their wellbeing comes first'
items.text:
What happens when our purrsonal ethics conflict with the biological needs of an animal we chose to care for?

There are a lot of things about cat ownership that become so normal you quickly furrget how objectively weird they are. You scoop their bathroom business into a plastic bag multiple times per day, you spend money on furniture specifically designed to be destroyed, and you quickly learn the difference between their different kinds of meows. One can mean "I'm hungry" and another can mean "I saw a bug a few hours ago and you must know about it." You fellow cat pawrents know what I'm talking about.

And then there is feeding them meat. I don't think anyone likes it. All the wet foods have this weird smell that, even after 12 years of owning cats, I still can't get over. Don't even get me started on the ingredients.

Most longtime cat pawrents probably do not think very deeply about it every time they crack open a can. Cats eat meat, that is simply part of the deal. For one brand-new kitten owner, though, that realization caused something of a moral meat crisis.

They eagerly went out and bought them high-quality kitten food while focusing on giving their baby the best pawssible start. Then, as a strict vegan, they realized that every can of cat food represented an ethical equation they had spent years trying to remove themselves from. Smartly, they did want to force their beliefs onto their kitten, but they also wondered whether there was another way to make it work.

And this is where I think the story gets really interesting, because this is something a lot of vegans deal with. And, we all know that people have a lot of feelings about veganism, whether it's for or against.

items.title: A Cozy Corner of Sleepy Kitty Memes Ready for a Cat Nap
items.text:
You are getting eepy, very eepy. Now, quick, grab your closest feline friend and take a nap! Do you feel better?

Of course you do! There is nothing better than taking a quick snooze with your favorite fur buddy. Not all cats are cuddlers, but all are definitely nappers. Cats can sleep anywhere from 12 to 16 hours a day! Talk about a cat nap… I wonder where that saying came from: "cat nap." Was it something more profound, or was it because humans saw that cats napped all day? Either way, it makes total sense. Cats like to nap! They are the ultimate bestie to get comfy cozy with. Watching a movie on a rainy night? That's pretty good, but now imagine that with a warm, purring kitten on your lap! See? So much better. Just got home from a long, stressful day of work and want to go brain silent for a bit and doomscroll? Well, do that guilt-free when there is a cat by your side just enjoying their cozy time with you. It's different with dogs. Canine companions are great because when you get home, they straight up run laps around the room because they are so happy to see you! But some people aren't at that level of energy, like some cat people. Some pet parents just want to come home and curl up in a blanket and chill. That's purrrrfect for a cozy kitty! And so are these memes.

items.title: A Sweet Stash of Cat Memes Offering a Little Treat Before Halloween
items.text:
Would Halloween have been half as exciting without the promise of candy?

When I was a kid, Halloween meant it was the time of the year to dress up in a spooky costume and go from house to house with my friends, asking for treats. People usually gave us something, so we got used to the dynamic. We knocked, someone opened the door and filled our pumpkins with candy. Excellent transaction. The best one ever invented. How could we not love Halloween?

I remember one Halloween it rained, and one of my friends' moms drove us around the neighborhood so we could still go trick-or-treating. I remember how happy I was that we didn't have to give up on the evening. We still got to visit houses and collect our treats because she took us. What a generous soul to spend part of her night helping a car full of children get more sugar. I'm still grateful. I hope she's doing well now and all her wishes came true!!

items.title: 11 small town red flags that show they're not a good place to live: 'One family owning 99% of the businesses'
items.text:
There are some places that make you want to leave as soon as you set foot in them.

If it is the kind of life that you want to lead, there is nothing wrong with deciding that a small town is the place for you. The houses are probably cheaper than a lot of other places, and it is a less hectic pace of life than being in the big city. Being somewhere where everybody knows everybody isn't going to appeal to some, but for others, it is exactly what they want.

No doubt about it, when it is done right, the small-town attitude can be charming enough for even the most hardened city slicker to rethink what it is they are doing in the big smoke. That's what every Hallmark movie has always taught us, right?

Unfortunately, this isn't the reality for every place that just so happens to have a reduced population. In fact, much of the time, the reason that a town doesn't have that many people is that so many felt like the best option was to leave it behind. It takes a real effort to make any town or city a good place to live, no matter what the size, but if that effort isn't there, it tends to be magnified in those places where there aren't as many inhabitants. The things that simply don't work so well are made pretty obvious, and it isn't even like there are enough neighborhoods for there to be a way to ignore the bad parts now and then.

items.title: 21 Romantic Memes to Send Your Loved One
items.text:
I may love you, but just saying it won't be enough for you to understand it.

Has it ever occurred to you that your loved one isn't fully aware of the fact that you love them, even though you have said it a million times already? It can be due to insecurities, trauma from a past relationship, or simple doubt caused by the sense of disbelief that someone could love them that much. Doubt and lack of assurance can have a thousand reasons to exist in someone's mind, but that doesn't mean that it should be like that. As a partner, if you realize that your loved one isn't fully sure about your love for them, you start to feel the need to prove it to them. As someone who has felt unloved even when the other person did, in fact, love me. In my first relationship, I couldn't believe that someone would ever love me for me; I was so insecure that I couldn't even imagine that sentiment that was being professed to me to ever be true. I can give you some relationship advice to make your other half aware that they are very much loved.

I was always very insecure, so a simple 'I love you' didn't really mean to me what the other person wanted it to mean. For me, it was a dumb phrase that could be said around without having any feelings attached to it. I saw it as a form of expressing that the other person was "fine" or "cool"; not that they loved me. For me to fully get into my mind that someone did love me, I needed to hear far more than that. Something that worked was for the other person to tell me exactly what went through their mind when they first met me and what they thought about when they saw me at that moment. That made me aware of what they think, which proves their love towards me. Another thing that I liked to hear, instead of their cliché phrase, was to know if they think about me when we are not together, what kind of situations made them think about me, and what they evoked in their mind.

There are other forms of showing love that work better for other people. Not everyone likes to make others explain that much about their feelings. Some people like gifts as a way to show love. Others prefer physical touch as a constant reminder of the love that the other person feels for them. Whatever they think that the best way of lovelanguage is, that is the way your will make them understand your love for them. A simple 'I love you' doesn't mean the same or have the same importance for everyone. You need to find the correct way of making your loved one aware of the love you are professing in a way that is understandable to them. Maybe some memes can work for them, using laughter as a way to get the true feelings out.

items.title: A pillowcase full of snoozy memes for all adults who want to leave everything behind and just use the afternoon for a long nap
items.text:
Don't you just love to have a good nap in the middle of the day and wake up all confused, not knowing what day it is?

I'm a firm believer in the fact that taking a nap solves half of your everyday life problems. Are you too tired from work? Take a nap. You argued with half of your family over some stupid thing? You're tired; take a nap. Do you feel like you go through life hating people, and that everybody has a natural talent to get on your nerves? Dude, really, go to sleep for an hour or two. I promise, naps have a way of resetting your life back to square one.

Every time I feel like I hate all of humanity, I lie down for a while, and when I wake up, I say, "Huh, maybe people aren't so evil." I swear to you, naps have kept me and countless other people from turning into the real-life version of the Midgard Serpent, ready to begin the end of the world. At this point, they should be considered World Heritage, since, you know, they have kept the universe alive and all of that.

Seriously, some days I just wake up in the morning and feel like I was run over by a truck; that's how tired I get, and what saves me from falling asleep in the middle of my workday? Taking a little nap. I promise, it will restart your existence and turn you into a much more energetic and productive person. And even if it doesn't, who doesn't like to spend the entire afternoon in bed doing absolutely nothing?

items.title: Mother buys daughter-in-law a dress from Spirit Halloween to wear to her husband's graduation: 'I didn’t ask for a dress'
items.text:
Sometimes a gift can be more than a gift. It can be a backhanded comment.

The way that we dress can be so personal to us. It reflects who we are and what we like and what we believe. If you're a person who takes stock in your style, you probably do a lot of thinking about it. You enjoy shopping and putting together outfits, and you enjoy the feeling you get when wearing something that you love outside of the house. This is why clothing is such a tricky gift to give somebody under any circumstance. Unless you know their exact size and exactly what they want, buying somebody a clothing item is always going to be a swing. It might be a swing and a hit, but it will more likely be a swing and a miss. It can be hard to define what you like about an item of clothing. You might like the way it feels on your body, the way it drapes, or it might remind you of a character that you love from movies or TV, or a moment from the past that you're trying to capture. It's hard to appear in somebody else's head and know what they're thinking about an item of clothing. This is why I generally avoid giving clothing as a gift. It's just way too risky. And you never know you might end up offending somebody by buying them something you think they would like, and they don't like. But more than that was happening here. This dress was an offense to anybody.

items.title: 25 Unexpected Animal Friends to Restore Your Faith in the Power of Friendship (October 24, 2026)
items.text:
How did you meet your friends?

I don't remember how I met my friends. Who said hello to whom, who made the first move? Who was brave enough to break the ice? I can't really pin back the exact moment when we decided we were going to be in each other's lives for a long time. I don't even remember when I decided I was going to call them friends. I truly believe that's what makes friendship so special. One day you just meet someone who resonates with you and, suddenly, they become part of your life. No agreement, no contract, no previous discussion; just two people drawn together organically and, most of the time, without a clear explanation. Now, I am very happy to confess that I don't even remember what my life used to be like without them.

That said, it is shocking how one instant can mold your life completely. I meet my friends on a weekly basis; I rely on them to give me advice, and it makes me happy to share time with them. What if we hadn't met? What if I had been distracted for that second of my life? That's why I don't think some friendships are unexpected. I think every single friendship is unexpected. I mean, what are the chances of meeting someone who complements you, who sends you excellent memes when you need to laugh, and who can understand your unspoken language? Call it luck, the universe, or destiny; it is truly an unexpected event.

This collection celebrates friendship. But mostly, it celebrates its unexpected nature, always coming to our lives when we need it the most, and when we expect it the least. Showing up uninvited and staying with us forever. Send this to your friends and remind them that meeting each other was a very fortunate and wholesome universal fluke.

items.title: 31 Fantasy Novel Memes About Getting Emotionally Attached to Dragons, Vampires and Fallen Angels
items.text:
Who else read fantasy novels and started expecting far too much from real life?

I started reading fantasy novels when I was a teenager. I'm thankful for the first time I walked into a bookstore, got captivated by a fantasy cover and decided to take it. The covers had this mysterious look, with hints of supernatural creatures and worlds very different from my own. I think that's what intrigued me most: the possibility of discovering a world where I had no idea what to expect. Those covers drew me in and then I fell in love with the stories. Soon, I was asking my mom for the next book in whatever series had taken over my life. She was encouraging a lovely hobby. And investing a lot of money too. Meanwhile, I was developing very unreal expectations about boys I might meet someday (and will never meet)

For a while, I was completely obsessed with vampires. If a series had vampires, that was enough to catch my attention. I could spend afternoons reading about mysterious characters with secrets and forbidden romances. Why didn't boys at my school have fangs? I was so sad when it finally sank in that I would never meet a vampire. And I wasn't going to become one either. It felt deeply unfair. Somebody should have mentioned that before I got emotionally involved.

items.title: ‘You’re doing the best you can, Mom and Dad!'A family gathering of parenting laughs for witty mothers and fathers (October 24, 2026)
items.text:
Ready for a very demanding Halloween?

I've gone on and on about how parenting is not easy. I don't think anyone doesn't know that by now. We don't even have to look at tired parents to know that, but it is enough to remember who we used to be as kids, and let me tell you, we were terrible. We ran around, broke things, fought our parents right before bedtime, and made as much chaos as possible whenever we could. The funny part is, those moments in which our parents probably wanted to punish us forever also happen to be some of the best memories we still hold as adults.

When I was a kid, for example, Halloween was coming, and I was very happy to go trick-or-treating with my friends. We were old enough to go on our own, and our parents had agreed to allow us to test our responsibility (in a closed residential area, of course). We were supposed to get back to my friend's home at exactly 8 pm. So, we started our trick-or-treating route, getting our bags filled with candy. In the meantime, we were also running around, telling each other spooky stories and competing on who could get more candy overall. That said, we completely failed our parents' test. By the time we decided to check the time, we were an hour late, and everyone's parents were furious ( understandably). We all got punished for weeks. But if you ask me, looking back, it was absolutely worth it.

I can only imagine how stressed my parents were when I disappeared with my friends for an hour on Halloween night. I can only imagine how exhausted they were after they had to take me to the doctor a couple of days later, because I got a stomachache from eating too much candy at once. I can't imagine at all how they managed to do it all over again for at least 15 years. That's why, as the spooky season is in full bloom now, here you've got a parenting meme list to prepare you for what's about to come. If you thought parenting was hard, just know that it gets a lot harder around the holidays and celebrations.

items.title: ‘Found Out Situationship Automated Our Chat, So I’ve Been Talking to an AI for Three Months’: 17 Dating Memes for Surviving Situationships
items.text:
Situationships, eye-contactships, and all the other ships we let sail away

They say a situationship is a situationship for one person and nothing for the other. I say it's a curse, and I always seem to be on the desperately in-love side, but never on the other.

The bad news is that situationships can break your heart just like any other relationship, even though they technically never existed. These relationships turn us into private investigators, and somehow we still get nothing in return; information is never enough when we're living in denial. But as Wendy Williams put it: "Denial is a river in Egypt," and that's all I have to say.

When we're inside these kinds of relationships, even though we're perfectly rational beings everywhere else, we turn into lunatics who believe that if we wait long enough, or accept low-effort long enough, the person we adore will finally love us with all their heart.

That they will result in no good becomes painfully easy to see for everyone else, but for us. Everyone has to go through one (or multiple) to finally learn the lesson.

But wait, I want to defend hopeless romantics for a second. Look, the situationship discourse tends to ridicule the person who falls in love, but what about the one who clearly sees that the other person is vulnerable and keeps feeding their hopes?

Let's not forget it takes two people to create a situationship. I've been in many relationships where I noticed the other person had more feelings for me than I did for them, and I'd always talk about it immediately and exit the relationship if I realized the other person was too in love to say no but actually wanted more.

I say there is responsibility on the low-commitment side of the situationship, and that we're focusing too much on the 'delusional' aspect of the romantic one and very little on the manipulative behaviours of the one getting all the attention and none of the responsibilities.

In this modern era, we read the person who doesn't feel anything as more mature, chic, and put-together; but do we really consider not forming attachments to people we hook up with as a goal? Isn't that a little problematic?

I know there isn't anything wrong with wanting intimacy with no commitment, but too many people focus on the 'saying it' part and think they're covered by just talking about it, even when their actions reflect the opposite, and it's completely normal for the other person to think love is flourishing when you're inviting them to dinner with your family.

So next time you want to call your friend who is in a situationship 'delusional', let's actually check the dynamics going on between them and try to help! Nobody deserves to wait to be loved; it's frankly better to be alone than to live hanging on false hope, even if it doesn't feel like it at first.

And if it's you who's going through a situationship, I wish you the best, and that all the love you gave returns to you multiplied. In the meantime, enjoy this meme list.

items.title: ‘Mostly, I hate the way I don’t hate you’: 10 Things I Hate About You Moments That We Too Can’t Hate, Not Even Close
items.text:
"Make anyone cry today?" Yeah, myself.

Some say film magic relies heavily on special effects and stunts. The wonders of cinematography, combined with the latest technological creations, bring us some of the best productions. Well, I couldn't disagree more. I don't think the magic of film has much to do with how it looks, but with how it makes us feel. Some of my favorite movies are quite low budget and have no impressive CGI explosions or complicated choreography. They are simply authentic. Their sheer honesty is what makes them, in my eyes, magical.

10 Things I Hate About You is one of them. I think movies and good stories come into your life exactly where they're supposed to. I was 14 years old, an angsty teenager with a lot of small-big problems trying to figure out how to be me. Thinking, like teenagers usually do, that there was a right way to grow into an adult, and anything far from that mold was not permitted. Trying to match the expectations of the world, and not my own. That's when I met Kat. A girl who was not afraid to speak her mind and show her true self. A girl who had some strong opinions about the world and had no problem sharing them. A true icon.

Today, 10 Things I Hate About You is 27 years old and, as much as life has changed for everyone, it still remains a masterpiece. It is time to dive back into it, remember what we loved in the first place, and revisit some of the very needed lessons these characters gave to us, just in case we forgot and need to be reminded. So, inspired by the unmatched Julia Stiles' creativity, enjoy this trip to one of the best times of our lives, with a list of the 26 Things I Love About This Wonderful Movie.

items.title: 24 Dog Memes Kicking Off an October Weekend With Good Boy Energy
items.text:
How does "I'm too tired to do anything" turn into "What time are we meeting?" so quickly on a Friday?

I would love an explanation, because it happens to me every time. I finish working, think about everything I have to study, and decide that my evening plans involve lying down. That's it. But then someone mentions going out for drinks or getting food together, and suddenly I'm thinking about what outfit I'm wearing tonight. So it turns out I wasn't finished for the day. I just needed to hear a good plan.

This is where I understand dogs perfectly. They get so excited when you suggest doing some plan with them. The plan: you grabbed the leash. I feel the same way when a friend suggests a cool plan. The only difference with dogs is that I don't run in circles. The excitement is of the same kind. Food and drinks with my favorite people? We're going somewhere nice? Oh, I'm listening. The week can wear me out, but I still get excited about spending a few hours with my friends. Especially when nobody expects me to have anything useful to say.

items.title: ‘If Earth Is Round, Then Explain This!!!’: 17 Age of Empires Memes That Bring Us Back to the Dark Ages
items.text:
Did we all take our responsibilities as rulers of an imaginary civilization in Age of Empires I too seriously?

I would always choose the Egyptians for some reason. Yes, I was one of those kids obsessed with Ancient Egypt, and I still am. I love that Age of Empires was secretly teaching us History. I didn't find history topics necessarily boring at school, but through the game, I was able to experience History in a very different way. I took my civilizations very seriously, and it made me feel like I was experiencing History in first person.

Ok, it might not have been as historically accurate; I mean, civilizations didn't evolve by collecting enough berries and clicking a button, but you get my point. Every time I see those simple graphics, I yearn for the long childhood afternoons I spent playing the game. The stakes were enormous.

The other day I was writing an article about The Sims' possible new AI developments, and it got me thinking about Age of Empires and how much the game could be developed with artificial intelligence. Land could finally be infinite!

But then again, would I actually want that?

Do you remember the WOLOLO! sound? I unlocked so many memories by sourcing these memes that I'm about to download the game and resume playing.

Age of Empires I is from 1997, so it's from an era where games didn't need cinematic storytelling or photorealistic graphics to be completely absorbing, and that's precisely what I like about them: the tiny pixelated people, the repetitive sounds, and the simple animations.

There is something incredibly charming about vintage computer games like Age of Empires. I love to play games like these; I specifically look for them. I've played Monkey Island I also recently, and I wouldn't change it for anything. I don't like the newer versions; I prefer the sort of arcade vibe, the limited possibilities, and the slow development.

Before we had any responsibilities, we had civilizations to run. Now I have responsibilities, but I think resuming my duties as ruler of Ancient Egypt is more important.

Though, just like I did with The Sims, I didn't play to win or achieve the perfect strategy; I just liked putting together pretty scenarios and exploring the game. I think these vintage games are enriched by their limitations; not everything gets better by using the newest technology. Maybe we don't want games to offer infinite possibilities; life already gives us too many possibilities, and we want games with boundaries to play inside.

All this made me think about Rollercoaster Tycoon; omg, the memories keep coming up. I think I already know what I'm going to do this weekend: I'll load my computer with all these vintage games, and won't leave the house.

I hope I come back here next week with a lot of memes and stories to write about. It will be like one of those long weekends when you didn't have school on Monday, except I'm 30 years old, and I'll have work.

items.title: The Most Entertaining Takes From TikTok This Week (October 24, 2026)
items.text:
When it comes to the business of scrolling, TikTok has the game figured out.

It somehow knows exactly how to cotton on to the specific interests and favored distractions of every user, and then feed them a stream of content that will keep them looking at their phone for hours on end. Even for those who don't use it, the way that screen dependency works in this day and age can at least partly be traced back to TikTok.

There is just something about frying your brain with a never-ending stream of short-form video that proves irresistible to millions of us, as proven by the fact that almost every major social platform out there has adopted a TikTok-like feature after the clock app's rise to prominence. It isn't just that so many of us are entranced by being able to watch all this; countless individuals are also willing to try their hand at entertaining the world by becoming an influencer, if that is even what we call them these days.

We have no choice but to be grateful, as it gives us a glut of amusing content whose influence extends far beyond the average For You page. The musings and antics of TikTokers everywhere are something anyone chronically online can relate to, and they can have fun with it. TikTok reminds us that there are a million different lives being lived out there by billions of people, and at the end of the day, all anybody wants is a little validation for their existence.

items.title: Tiny dachshund puppies come bouncing toward the camera in the sweetest little stampede: 'Can I have… all of them?'
items.text:
Is there a better welcome than a puppy running toward you when you get home?

I would happily accept that reception every time I walked through my front door. Even if I'd only gone out to buy bread. Yes, I was gone for ten minutes, but these doggos greet you like they've been waiting for you all day. And if I had a thousand dachshunds, I would love the full reunion every time I get home. Being greeted with so much enthusiasm before you've even had a chance to put your things down makes you feel like someone is longing to see you, that your presence matters, and that you are special. Because you really are to your dog. And he literally has been waiting for you all day. Please pet him.

When I was little, I had a dog I named Cookie. I loved the way he would follow me around the house. I read a lot of books as a kid, and one of my favorite things was finding a sunny spot outside when the weather was nice and lying on the grass with whatever book I was reading at that moment. Cookie would come along and lie down beside me. So I was happy reading there with him next to me. It wasn't an activity that required dogs, but he joined me anyway, and having him there made the activity feel even nicer. I could get absorbed in what was happening on the page while he kept me company. Every now and then, my attention would come back to the little dog beside me, and I'd feel so pleased that he'd decided to stay. Reading was something I loved, and he made himself part of it by staying close.

items.title: Spooky Memes Because Halloween is Almost Here and We Couldn't Be More Excited
items.text:
We've been waiting for Halloween all year round, and now it's almost here! Ready for the spookiest night of all?

Is it just me, or does October feel like the longest month when you're waiting for Halloween? I have to confess, I've been waiting for this time of year since late September. As soon as October 1st hit my calendar, I was already ready for candy, home decor, and costume ideas. I get so excited whenever I see grocery stores stocking up on all that candy… I feel like a child again, and honestly, that's what Halloween is all about. Feeling like a kid and getting excited about dressing up and eating candy is a nice little break from adult reality, and I very much appreciate it.

That's why time seems to be slowing down when we're reaching the spookiest day. But, luckily for us, the day still has 24 hours, so it's just the excitement in our heads that makes us feel that time isn't really moving. Needless to say, we're a week out of Halloween, and the vibes are getting scarier. In fact, I see people trying on costumes, buying some home decorations, and debating whether to give trick-or-treaters candy or prepare a healthy snack. Can you guess my answer? I think it's pretty obvious. Imagine ringing the doorbell and having the family give you apples and carrot sticks… please, just don't.

items.title: 33 Aussie wildlife memes (mostly) for those Australians out there just trying to survive every time they step outside
items.text:
G'day mate! I've got a bit of something for you to think about.

For most of us, when we head out of the house, we're worried about three things: keys, wallet, phone. Checking each necessary pocket to make sure we have life's essentials. But for Aussies, when it's late in the arvo and you want to pop on your thongs and trackies to pop out in the ute and head down to the servo, you have so much more you have to worry about.

I'd have to imagine that when you head out the door in Australia you're looking over your shoulder, watching for some spider that looks like Shelob from Lord of the Rings to drop down on your head. Simultaneously, checking your ankles for any snakes that might be lurking about. Then you have to dodge past the swooping magpie as you duck under the old tree out front and box a kangaroo before you can finally jump into the ute and tear out. items.title: 'I'm still crying': Fans are still emotional and thrilled after Julia Stiles' tribute performance at Dancing With the Stars
items.text:
I'm not crying; you are… Alright, we're all crying. It's not every day that we get to see people using dance to honor their loved ones.

I got to see Julia Stiles' performance on Dancing With the Stars, and yes, I was one of those crying my eyes out. I confess it made me really emotional to see that she and her partner were referencing one of the most iconic romcoms ever, and Julia's costar in that movie. Her hairstyle, her dress, even some of the dance moves were a direct reference to Heath Ledger and one of the most iconic dance scenes ever choreographed.

I recently rewatched 10 Things I Hate About You, and let me tell you, I loved it as much as I did when I watched it for the first time. I always related to Kat's attitude towards people's expectations and the unapologetic way in which she expressed her opinions. For a 90s movie, it was surprisingly advanced, and it had a good deal of well-written female characters, which is not little to say about most movies, even today. Kat had a defined personality, wishes and aspirations of her own, and never let other people dictate the way she thought and behaved. In comparison to other main characters, she was a great role model for young women, even with her slightly aggressive nature.

Obviously, I'm not the only one who is still a fan of the movie and absolutely loved the performance. All these people on Twitter were thrilled to see Julia and the rest of the cast return for this tribute!

items.title: Malicious Coworker Keeps Taking Credit for Other People’s Work: ‘By the third time, I started keeping copies of everything I sent’
items.text:
When your coworker is a credit thief

Some people have mastered the art of looking busy while secretly looking for ways to steal credit from those who are actually doing real work. Don't get me wrong; they invest a lot of energy in it, and it becomes a full-time job, but it would be more ethical to invest all that energy into actually working.

They'll be the first to volunteer to present work and say, "We've been working so hard on this," while everyone thinks: "We?" At first, it might go unnoticed, but reality always catches up to them, and everyone on the team ends up hating them and/or taking revenge.

Many office achievements are reserved for those who successfully advertise their accomplishments, not necessarily for those who objectively accomplish more.

These credit thieves are generally very quick to put the "I" in work they never participated in, and even quicker to throw a "we" when there is a mistake. It's all about enhancing their good qualities and hiding those not so good. We all do it, to some extent, but there are limits.

They usually take advantage of the fact that not many people like conflict or confronting others, and they use that to thrive. But if they steal credit long enough, it will likely backfire, and when it does, every team member will be there, happily watching.

At work, your intellectual credit can grant you a better position, more responsibility, more money, and many other cool improvements. The thing is, eventually, if a credit thief gets any of those, they won't be able to perform at a higher level, and that's when the mask will drop. You can't steal your way out of work as you go up the ladder and take more responsibility; at some point you are going to be confronted with actual work, and you won't know what to do.

I have to say it, I actually believe in confronting people, and I don't understand why it has such a bad reputation. I've done it many times, and when you do it on time and assertively, it can save you years of stress and petty fights.

I used to have a friend in college who copied my every move, to the point that it became weird to everyone but her. At first, I didn't say anything because I thought it was my imagination, but when it became evident, I immediately brought it up to her, and it was like the spell was broken. Of course she denied it, but it probably made her so embarrassed that she dropped it the next day.

Confrontation works wonders, if you do it well. If I had to give you advice on that, I would say you have to be very respectful and try to keep it short and to the point. The most important thing is that what's bothering you stops being a weird taboo that grows without anyone noticing.

Once you put it on the table, you can do something about it. So good luck confronting anyone you have to confront!

items.title: Medical Receptionist Job Posting Requires Applicants Have 15-30 Years of Experience, Despite Only Paying $16-19 an Hour
