What kind of people are applying to this job? Or was the posting written by a bot that intended for bots to apply for it?

Have you ever looked at a job posting and wondered, "Who in their right mind would apply to such a position?" I'm talking about jobs where employees only make $45K a year in San Francisco and are expected to work around the clock. Some jobs require 10-15 years of experience and still pay only $70K in New York City. If you're a normal person who is trying to pay your bills and put some money away for retirement, these jobs probably don't sound like they're for you, and you're probably right. A lot of jobs exist for the sole purpose of employing independently wealthy young people who don't need an income from a job to pay their bills. If someone has a hefty trust fund that gives them enough money to live more than comfortably every year without having to lift a finger, then they can easily take a "fun" job that makes no money. Such positions are not limited to young rich people; they also exist for old rich people.

items.title: It's Furiday Night And These Cool Cats Are Meowt On The Town
items.text:
It's Furiday night, and we're going out! We've spent all week looking forward to seeing our friends, getting out of the house, and having some fun. But as we're getting ready to leave, our cat is sitting by the door, looking suspiciously interested in coming along.

Now, most cats would probably hate the idea of a night out. They're perfectly happy staying home, sleeping on the couch, and enjoying having the entire house to themselves. But some kitties are surprisingly social. They love meeting new people, exploring new places, and getting involved in whatever their humans are doing.

And we have to admit, bringing your cat along on a Furiday night sounds pretty entertaining.

For starters, you'd immediately become the most popular person in your friend group. Nobody would care what you've been up to all week once they spotted a cat hanging out with you. Everyone would want to say hello, take pictures, and ask a million questions about your furry companion. You might as well accept that you're no longer the main attraction.

We also wonder what cats would think of our usual Friday night conversations. Imagine sitting around with your friends, catching up on everyone's latest drama, while your kitty listens from the next seat. They'd probably have some pretty strong opinions about everything, judging by the looks they give us at home.

Then there's the matter of finding somewhere comfortable to sit. We all know how picky cats can be about their favorite spots. You could find the nicest seat in the place, only for your feline friend to decide they'd rather sit directly on your lap. And once they've settled in, you're probably not going anywhere for a while.

The photos alone would make the evening worthwhile. We'd be taking pictures of our cats posing with everyone, looking around curiously, and generally being the cutest members of the group. Forget taking a normal group picture. We'd want the cat in every single one.

Naturally, we'd only bring along a kitty who's comfortable being out and about, with a secure carrier or harness and somewhere quiet to retreat if needed. Plenty of cats would much rather stay home, and we can't blame them.

But for those outgoing little felines who love an adventure, why shouldn't they join the Furiday night fun? We spend enough time talking about our cats when we're out with friends anyway. We might as well bring them along and let everyone meet the celebrities themselves.

items.title: 31 Feline Funnies for People Raising Ruckus Cat Children
items.text:
Some cats are just wilder than others.

There are cats who can sit on your lap all day long, only taking food and bathroom breaks because they have to - and then returning to steal some more of your body warmth (and your heart). But then there are the absolute demons, the spawns of satan who were probably pspspsed here during a dark summoning ritual. My cat is not like that. Sure, she has the occasional zoomies trip in the middle of the night, but she's not the complete ruckus mess some other cats are. My friend's cat, though… he's another story completely.

Way before I had a cat of my own, I took a vacation for a month, and it just so happened that this friend needed a place to stay. I sublet my room to her and her cat. She warned me he's a wacky one, and this wasn't news - I already heard the stories about him directly from her. The Prophet was his name. Well, Elijah initially, but the more character he's shown as he grew up, the more it became clear he needed his own title. So… Elijah The Prophet, yes? He's an absolute maniac.

When I came back home after the sublet/vacation period, I returned to a room I did not recognize. The curtains were rolled up above the window, the computer was on the highest shelf of my closet (yes, inside), and the office chair was shredded to pieces. That was the art exhibition The Prophet left me. Or, more accurately, his hooman. The chair thing was inevitable, but the curtains and my PC were thoughtfully well-defended. But with that being said, I don't think I'm about to host that crazy cat in my house ever again. At least the story I was left with is funny, as are all this cat's other stories.

items.title: Teacher calls out fellow teachers, claims students notice when they use AI: 'I love your homemade notes'
items.text:
Since when did it become acceptable for teachers to outsource the knowledge they were hired for?

It is no secret that most people cut corners in their job now and then, and just because they are responsible for educating the nation's children doesn't mean that teachers are any exception. I mean, most former students of a certain age have fond memories of when the TV got wheeled in to watch a movie. The education system has seen its fair share of slacking off from both kids and adults.

The difference between teaching now and doing it even just a few years ago is that artificial intelligence tools are now widely available, and educators who don't feel like coming up with their own lesson plan can get the computer to do it instead. Given that this technology is known for making many mistakes and Gen Alpha is probably the generation best equipped to tell when something is AI-generated, teachers have good reasons to avoid AI when they can. Unfortunately, schools across the land prove that this isn't the case.

Teaching isn't an easy profession, and it is only more challenging with the full-blown literacy crisis that many believe we are experiencing right now. Still, that doesn't mean that potentially making it worse by relying on AI as a teaching assistant is the right way to go. Burnout is real, but so is seeing kids become even more checked out because it seems like ChatGPT is more invested in their education than the person right in front of them.

items.title: 'Laughter is the best medicine': 34 Laughs That Will Guide You On Your Inner Journey to a Happy Brain This Weekend (October 23, 2026)
items.text:
How are you doing? So-so? Not so good? Wondering when you enlisted to be the universe's strongest soldier? Yep, don't worry. You're not alone!

The internet has a lot of dark places and toxic traits, but there is one magical trait that we can all agree is the best part: unity. You never feel alone on the internet because it turns out people are struggling the same way you are; these memes are proof! Your therapist would suggest journaling, meditating, or maybe talking to friends and family. However, it's 2026; you can do all of that while staring at a screen! Heck, you can even see your therapist through your screen. I guarantee you, whatever you are struggling with, there was someone who made a meme about it a decade ago. See? You're never alone! But you don't want to get caught in the doomscroll of it all, so take this finite list and make your therapist proud!

items.title: 'What’s a financial mistake that can take years to recover from, even if you earn a decent salary?': People discuss what the biggest financial mistake they ever committed was
items.text:
Have you ever encountered money problems due to a financial mistake you made? Did you learn anything from it?

Money problems are common, especially with the current state of the world. People get into debt more and more, whether it is to buy a house, a car, go to college, or for medical expenses. Almost everything can make you need a loan and put you in debt. I'm not here to demonize loans. They are a good way to go through life and do and have the things you want without having to save for your whole lifetime before acquiring them. But they only work out if you are extremely careful with your finances, you cannot trust them to just work out eventually; you need to plan, have stability, and have as your main goal to pay them out.

Nobody learns how to manage their finances unless they studied something related to that in college; it's not common knowledge. In school, you don't learn about credit cards, debt, loans, or even budgeting. So the only two ways you actually learn what to do with your money are by getting some tips from your parents or family members, or by making mistakes. The last one is the most common. People learn how to manage after already committing the mistakes that put them in money issues, and recovering is hard. That's why it is important to listen to what others have gone through as a way to learn not only from their mistake, but also how to recover from them. It can be stressful to have issues with your finances, but it's important to remember that you are not alone. A lot of people go through the same things. In the U.S., according to National Debt Relief, more than 45% of citizens have credit card debt, more than 35% have car loans, and more than 20% have student loans. So it's not uncommon to have debt. On the contrary, it is not that common to be debt-free. They explained that according to their data, only 23% of Americans are completely debt-free.

"Most Americans have long had some level of debt, and if you've taken on more due to the rapid rise in the cost of living"

What we should take from all this is that being in debt is not bad in itself. You can get into debt like most people in the U.S. and not be in financial trouble. That is how the economy of the country works. The problem is when you have debt but no way of paying, or too much debt in categories like credit cards that have insane interest rates. So, if you are in debt, you are not alone, not at all. A lot of people are in the same situation. The important thing isn't the debt, is to have a plan to pay it and be aware of the interests they have to prioritize what to pay first. Financial mistakes happen, but not everything has to be a tragedy. There is a way to solve the problems; we just need to learn how to manage money most constructively to avoid them happening again.

items.title: 'To the person who loved my cat before': Person writes a heartfelt letter to their cat's previous owner who loved the cat but had to let him go to a new home
items.text:
Rehoming a cat, sometimes, is the kindest choice.

Generally, of course, we are against cats being rehomed. There are so many solutions to so many issues that can be found. Letting your cat go should always be the last choice. Because as smart as cats are, they are still just cats, and they don't understand rehoming. They just think that they were abandoned by their owners. But sometimes, when the problem is insurmountable, surrendering your cat is not only the right choice, it's also the kindest one.

We always say that people should adopt a cat when they are ready, when they have enough stability in their lives. If that stability is gone, and if it can't be brought back, then you should not have a cat. It's simple to understand, but it's not easy to do. Of course, people do it all the time. We could write stories about abandoned cats every day, and we wouldn't run out. The only thing that we ask is that if you have to do it, do it right. Don't throw your indoor cat onto the street to fend for themselves. Find them another home if you can, and if you can't, take them to a shelter. So that they have an actual chance to be found by a new person who will love them just as much as you did. Like the person in today's story loves this cat.

items.title: 25+ Scooby Doo Memes for Friend Groups of 5 Dressing Up as Scooby, Shaggy, Fred, Velma, and Daphne for Halloween (October 24, 2026)
items.text:
What's new, Scooby-Doo? This list of Scooby-Doo memes is new and perfect for this spooky season, when villains, monsters, and ghouls are peeking around every corner.

Since I became an adult, I have seen friend groups of 5 dress up as the Mystery Gang for Halloween. If you have a mixed-gender millennial friend group, it's a classic go-to, and everyone seems to love it. Even though I like Scooby-Doo as much as the average person, I can't say that I love Mystery Gang group costumes. In fact, I despise them. I think it is probably the least creative costume that you can do, and that's coming from somebody who has dressed up as a witch for Halloween in my past.

As someone who's been in a friend group of 5, I understand the urge to dress up as the Mystery Gang. It makes it much easier because you don't have to buy super crazy new clothes. If you're Velma, you can go down to the local Rainbow Clothing, get a turtleneck, a skirt, and socks, and call it a day! Even better, you can integrate some of those pieces into your regular wardrobe once the holiday passes. If you're in a friend group that's lazy enough to do a Scooby-Doo group costume, they're probably not going to demand that you get a Velma wig or accurate glasses. As long as you stand next to your friends in similarly accurate costumes, everyone will know exactly who you are. It's perfect for people who don't care enough about Halloween to actually try!

One of the worst parts about dressing up as The Mystery Gang for Halloween is that one of you has to be Scooby. If one of you wants to be Scooby, that's fine, but I'd venture to say most girls don't want to be the dog when their bestie is Daphne. I've seen some pretty egregious group costumes where the four white friends made their one black friend dress up as Scooby, which is just plain wrong. Even if Scooby isn't the undesirable character for your particular friend group, somebody is going to be disappointed. Somebody is not going to want to be Velma because they don't think she's cute, and it's going to become a whole thing. Some guy will complain about wearing his Fred ascot all night long at the party, and once he takes it off, he'll just look like a blonde guy in a rugby shirt.

If you're going to dress up as a Scooby-Doo character, you should at least do something creative! Go as The Hex Girls with your group of friends! Go as hot Velma from Scooby-Doo 2: Monsters Unleashed, or as Scooby dressed up like an old woman on the plane. If you totally disagree with me and still want to go through with your Mystery Gang group costume, I can't stop you. All I hope is that my tirade won't stop you from enjoying this list of Scooby-Doo memes. They are Scrappy-Doo-free, if that means anything to you.

items.title: Grandma gets bamboozled by the price of gas when granddaughter reveals the price to fill up: 'You think my gas cost $10?'
items.text:
Must be nice to be completely unaware of the financial realities of modern life!

Old age supposedly comes with more wisdom, but one of the biggest drivers of generational rifts between young people, baby boomers, and even older generations is that they seem allergic to understanding the realities of being a youngish adult in today's world. Sure, there are Zoomers and millennials who could do with giving a bit more sympathy to their elders, and there are older people who can empathize with the fact that things just aren't as simple as they were back in their day. Nonetheless, even the well-meaning can sometimes have a conception of the lives of youth today that couldn't be further from the truth.

We have all heard the complaints about avocado toast, but the misinformation goes even further than that. The reason that some believe an innocent brunch snack is getting in the way of their grandkids affording to buy a house is that they genuinely think that starter homes are close to the same price they were when they were the target market. This isn't to say that older people didn't have their struggles, too, but it is the unwillingness of many to understand the problems faced by those still trying to make it in the world that can leave them shocked when they are faced with the cold, hard facts. Even an expense as simple as the price of a tank of gas can be enough to expose how they are out of touch.

items.title: The Best Heartwarmingly Wholesome Memes and Posts of the Week (October 22, 2026)
items.text:
The world can always make room for a little more niceness.

Too many people spend too much of their time sweating the small stuff and feeling overwhelmed by things that ultimately don't matter that much. When it comes down to it, the fundamentals of being happy are simple; we want to be comfortable, well fed, and feel loved and appreciated. It may be true that many of these things come as a struggle at times, but that doesn't mean that anybody should lose themselves to negativity. There is always a way to look on the bright side.

This attitude is what is fundamental to the practice of wholesome memes. We have to take a look around us and truly appreciate every opportunity where goodness strikes. We can sometimes come across it in the most unexpected of places, and also, the classic examples are easier to come by than some would have us believe. Being open to making it happen is the main thing.

One of the best things about living in the internet age is that no matter what may be going on in our lives, we have constant access to a varied stream of positivity if we know the right place to look. The doomscroll truly has nothing on this. If nothing else, we can be reminded that there are enough people experiencing good things all over the world for there to be enough wholesome content for everybody to enjoy. That is something special, even if we have long accepted it as normal.

items.title: 25+ Pancake Memes That Are Better Than Waffles (October 23, 2026)
items.text:
Pancakes and waffles can coexist in harmony, but for this meme list, pancakes reign supreme, and always will! Although the famous meme says that liking pancakes doesn't mean you hate waffles, this meme list is waffle-hater-friendly.

When I was growing up, my family often made pancakes, either on Saturday morning or as a breakfast-for-dinner main course. My younger sister was really good at making pancakes, and decided to make her own IHOP for the family. Instead of "International House of Pancakes," she operated "Catie's House of Pancakes," and CHOP was born.

The funniest thing about CHOP was the sizing. You could order pancakes in six different sizes: small, extra small, large, extra large, medium, and extra medium. Naturally, my parents had a field day with the "extra medium" label. My dad would order his pancakes "super extra medium," and my sister didn't understand why they found that so funny. For a while, I didn't either. After all, isn't extra medium just a size between medium and small? I thought my sister was pretty innovative. After all, no restaurant before CHOP had ever been daring enough to introduce an "extra medium" size, and she continued to offer extra medium pancakes, even when they were mocked.

Now that I don't live with my sister and her incredible pancake-making skills, I don't get to eat as many pancakes as I'd like. Even though I'm not eating pancakes today, scrolling through these pancake memes is better than nothing! Maybe I can even scroll through them at a diner that serves breakfast all day while munching on a stack of flapjacks! After all, I do have free will.

items.title: 12 employees share the fastest times they've seen a coworker get fired at their workplace: 'Intern used their corporate credit card to BUY a Honda civic.'
items.text:
Even if you feel like you make stupid mistakes at your job, I am almost certain that you haven't made as many stupid mistakes as the people who have gotten fired less than 24 hours after their first day of work.

The first year of a new job can be stressful. You know that if anything really bad happens to the company, you're going to be the first one to go. All the stuff they told you in the interview about how the company is growing and successful could be patently untrue, and if you aren't able to figure that out before you accept the job, you very well might be signing up to be on the cutting room table within a few short months of getting hired.

If you get hired at a good company, they will understand you won't be perfect at your brand-new job after 3 months. Every employee makes mistakes, and a good manager will guide you rather than reprimand you too harshly for normal mistakes. That said, you should have a solid grasp of your job's daily duties and responsibilities by 3 months in. Your boss shouldn't have to tell you to put on your safety equipment or remind you to schedule 5 newsletters per day if those are basic duties in your job description. Heck, you should know the basic duties of your job before you even walk in the door on day one, because they were probably listed on the job application or discussed in the interview!

In your first week at a new job, you have to mess up pretty badly to get fired. The people in this story got fired almost immediately after getting hired in most of the cases; I 100% understand why.

items.title: Couple rescues terrified kitten from neighboring building, and she attaches herself to the woman asking for constant cuddles and uppies: ‘She trusts me 100%’
items.text:
Have you ever had a cat with attachment issues? Cats are not usually very clingy, but sometimes they choose their hoomans as their safe space.

When an animal has been abandoned, it's usual for them to have trust issues in relation to human beings. After all, they were the ones who abandoned them in the first place. Both cats and dogs alike can be scared, reluctant to trust and jumpy before any kind of strange noise.

I've seen rescued cats and dogs behaving in the same way. The first week my kitty was at home after she was rescued, she was terrified. She opened her eyes round and wide as two full moons; her ears were always up, and she turned her head form one side to the other. All she did was cuddle in the couch and sleep, and every time someone made the smallest of noises, she would run away and hide under the couch. We couldn't even open the front door without her getting scared and hiding. It took her a few weeks to get used to the sounds of the house, and even months to start trusting us an behaving like a regular cat. She wouldn't meow at first either! She was so silent, as if she was afraid thta, if we noticed she was there, we would hurt her. It breaks my heart to remember it, but luckily, now she's all better.

Now, she meows normally, although she's not the most talkative. She always gets the zoomies, and plays around the house. She's even starting to misbehave! Now, I can't stop her from scratching the furniture or jumping all over the dining table. Seriously, if anyone has the number of a good cat trainer, please, send it to me. I'm getting desperate, and now I can't get her to quit her bad habits.

In this case, this couple rescued a girl cat who was terrified, and in bringing her to their home, she chose the woman as her source of protection. Now, she won't leave her alone, and she follows her everywhere.

items.title: 24 Pupper Pawsts to Put Some Doggo Sunshine on Your Soul
items.text:
Some dreary autumn days need extra sunshine, and that is easily attained by having a dog by your side.

A new dog has visited us in the office today! Her name is Batgirl, she's big and strong, fur is a slick black coat (hence her name), but she's the cowerdest cutie we've ever seen here. We already know all the regular dogs around our offices, and they already know us. But sometimes a new dog will come - an employee's relatives couldn't find a dog sitter, someone's spouse will come with their dog for the first time, or a new employee who introduces us to their doggo friendo. There are many reasons a new dog will find their way to our humble workplace - and we welcome each and every one of them.

And today, of all days, it was really needed. It was pouring outside - the autumn skies have finally opened the door to what would soon become winter's rain. We couldn't even go outside to bring lunch. But Batgirl was here. At first, she didn't leave her hooman's side, glued to her like a kangaroo joey in the pouch. But we had a plan with her person - every hour we would each approach gently with a snack, until she felt safe to run around us asking for more. I was third in line. It took me a minute, but Batgirl ate the snack directly from my hand. What a cutie.

After lunch, she agreed to come out of the table and receive gentle pets from everybody. Gently, slowly, but she agreed. This was truly the ray of sunshine we all needed on this dreary day - and it seems like Batgirl needed that no less than we did. Because loving dogs is a two-way street - we show them love, but they show it to us as well. That's the absolute magic of dogs, and I'm so thankful to have such adorable doggos in my life. I hope Batgirl will return for another visit soon.

items.title: 24 Rex-cellent Dinosaur Memes Embracing Each New Day With Roar-some Fun
items.text:
All animals are awesome, even if they're long gone and all that's left of them lives in backyard chickens.

Look, dinosaurs are cool. Every kid had a dinosaur phase. If you didn't have one, what kind of childhood did you even have? My favorite dinosaur was the Ankylosaurus. It's the heavily armored one with a tail that looks like a hammer and spikes all over its back. They were like the tanks of the Cretaceous period, which is the one that saw everything end when the dinosaurs went extinct around 66 million years ago. When I think about it now, it all fits with the fact that my favorite starter Pokémon was Bulbasaur - I just like the stocky and tanky things.

Besides paleontologists, who made dinosaurs their actual bread and butter, most of us grew out of this phase. But it doesn't mean none of us ever stopped liking dinosaurs. I still think they're really cool. Megafauna that ruled the Earth for a gajillion million years - how could they not be cool in anyone's eyes? Well, maybe I didn't grow out of my dinosaur phase completely. I might not know to tell you all the cool facts about them, like the actual dinosaur kid you've had in class (everybody had one), but I honestly still think they're the coolest creatures to have ever roamed the Earth.

And besides, we're animal lovers here. We can easily admit that all animals should be loved equally. Yes, even the weirdest animals out there in the wild. Every living thing deserves some love from animal lovers. So I bring some love to dinosaurs today, in the form of a bunch of memes every animal lover can enjoy. Because dinosaurs are so coooooool! They deserve to be appreciated by everyone. And it doesn't matter that they're not here anymore.

items.title: 26 Assorted Animal Memes to Sort the Sweetness of Your Day
items.text:
Do animals know that we love them so much?

I sometimes wonder if animals understand that all the self-described animal lovers actually do love them so much. Because when I think of wild animals, for example, I think of all the skittish ones who keep a fair distance from people, society, and civilization. But they have their good reasons, of course - it's not easy living as someone whose natural habitat keeps getting smaller and smaller each year, especially when you can't understand why. But that important conversation aside, it's not just the wildlings in nature - it's also our pets. All our dogs, cats, guinea pigs, hamsters - do they understand we love them like no other thing in this world? Do all our pets, snacks, and kisses convey this message to them clearly? I really want to know if they feel this love just as much as we feel it when we give it to them. It's important to me both as a pet owner and a general animal fan.

Regardless of the immense love animal lovers feel for all things living with fur, feathers, gills, and otherwise - there's always a fair chance that all animal lovers also love animal memes. So while I can't really understand if all the animals would ever know how much we love them, I can always enjoy the best content online, which is animal memes. Just any animal, really. It can be a majestic horse just as much as it can be a cute lil' bug. It can be a homebound animal like a cat, or a wild bear on fat bear week. Every animal counts, and every animal deserves love.

While you enjoy these animal memes, take a moment to think for a second - How do you show love to animals? Which animals could be shown more love? What can you do to make sure animals feel the love? And how awesome pawsome are animal memes actually, right? That's a lot to ponder about - let's get on with the memes themselves.

items.title: Woman worries her cat won't accept his new kitten sister until she catches them cuddling in the cutest way
items.text:
Getting a second cat is always a bit of a gamble. You hope your resident kitty will be thrilled to have a new friend, but there's also the possibility they'll spend the next six months hissing at each other from opposite ends of the couch. Some cats love having company, while others seem purrsonally offended that you've brought another animal into their home without consulting them first.

When two cats really hit it off, though, it's hard to beat watching their friendship develop. One day they're cautiously sniffing each other, and a few weeks later, they're grooming each other's faces and refusing to sleep separately. You'll buy them two perfectly good cat beds, only to find both cats squeezed into the same one. Apparently, having a best friend means never having to respect personal space again.

Kittens tend to take this arrangement particularly seriously. They're still figuring out how the world works, and having an older cat around gives them someone to follow, wrestle with, and generally annoy. The older cat might not have signed up for babysitting duties, but that doesn't stop the little one from treating them like a combination of parent, playmate, and climbing equipment.

That's exactly the situation Willie Nelson has found himself in since his human brought home a tiny kitten named Nene Leakes.

Nene arrived in August, when she was reportedly smaller than a baked potato. Her human worried about how Willie would handle having a baby sister. Would he get jealous? Would he miss being the only cat? Would the two of them even get along?

A recent update suggests that Willie has adjusted just fine, although he's apparently lost the right to nap alone.

Nene has taken to sleeping directly on top of her big brother, despite having plenty of other places to curl up. Sometimes she sprawls across him like a blanket, and sometimes Willie rests his chin on her. Their human describes them as taking turns being the furniture, which seems like a pretty accurate assessment of the situation.

We have to give Willie credit for his patience. Kittens aren't exactly known for choosing convenient places to sleep, and Nene seems determined to make herself comfortable wherever her brother happens to be lying.

It's especially sweet that she feels so comfortable around him. She's gone from being a tiny newcomer to having a built-in best friend who doesn't seem to mind being used as a mattress.

Their human may be responsible for the food and cleaning, but Willie and Nene have clearly decided they've got everything else covered.

items.title: Retired dad who insisted he wasn't a cat person now sends his family daily updates about his new feline friend
items.text:
Every family has that one dad who insists they're never getting a pet. He doesn't want fur on the furniture, doesn't want another mouth to feed, and definitely doesn't want an animal following him around the house. He's perfectly happy without one, thank you very much. But we've all seen how quickly that attitude can change.

It usually starts with a few complaints. The dog is too loud, the cat is scratching the couch, and somebody needs to explain why there's pet hair on his favorite shirt. Then, slowly, the complaints become less frequent. He starts asking whether the cat has eaten yet. He saves a little space beside him on the couch. Eventually, he's referring to himself as the animal's dad without a hint of irony.

The best part is that these dads rarely admit they've changed their minds. They'll insist they're only feeding the cat because nobody else remembered, or that they're letting it sleep on their lap because they don't want to disturb it. Meanwhile, everyone else in the family can see exactly what's happening.

One recently retired dad had no plans to join the pet-parent club. He'd never wanted an animal, especially a cat, but a scruffy little visitor apparently had other ideas.

The cat started showing up at his house and kept returning for several weeks. He looked underweight and worn, so the family wondered whether he might belong to someone nearby. They put the word out, hoping to find his owner, but nobody claimed him.

Eventually, Dad gave the cat a name: Bob. And apparently, Bob decided he'd found his person.

Now, the two spend their mornings together at the kitchen table. Dad drinks his coffee while Bob settles into his favorite corner, enjoying head scratches and cuddles as they watch the birds outside.

His family now receives daily pictures and videos of Bob, courtesy of the man who never wanted a cat in the first place.

We'd love to know how many photos it takes before someone officially loses the right to call themselves a pet hater. Surely, sending daily updates about your cat's activities qualifies.

Retirement probably looks a little different from what this dad originally imagined. Instead of enjoying a completely pet-free house, he's got a furry companion who apparently expects to join him for coffee every morning.

Judging by how inseparable they've become, we doubt Dad would have it any other way.

items.title: 25 Adorable Wild Animal Memes for Feral Friday Fun
items.text:
Nature is full of adorable creatures we can always learn something from, especially if it's wildlife inspiring our weekend plans.

Before every weekend, I look at the plans I made and try to imagine what the wild animals of the world would do to make them better. Not that wild animals know what the concepts of weekend or plans are, but I know that if I look at it through the glasses of nature, I get to have a much better weekend than I would've otherwise had. Let me demonstrate:

First, Friday night. Because if you can start your weekend earlier, why wouldn't you? It's not like I have any work or responsibilities on the night of a Friday. On the contrary - I'm going to celebrate the weekend with friends. We're going out together after not meeting for a while, so I'm quite excited. When I'm getting ready tonight, I'm thinking of swans. They're beautiful and elegant, fitting for a Friday night out inspiration. Unlike the peacock, that looks like it's trying too hard, a swan gives a sense of poise and rationality, and generally a fun someone to be around.

After a late Friday night, I'll probably need some time to recover all that spent energy - and that's what Saturdays are for. I plan to do absolutely nothing. And for that, I'm keeping in mind the manatee. These beautiful ocean blobs sleep for up to 12 hours a day, which sounds like a great plan to start the day with. When they're awake, they take things slowly, grazing the sea floor with absolute calm like true Saturday queens. That's exactly the energy I want to take with me on this Saturday - which is zero energy. Manatees are perfection for that.

And once I have all that energy back, it's time to spend it and make sure this weekend isn't wasted. And that's when Sunday comes into the picture - it's the day for actually making something. A hike, a visit, any sort of plan. This Sunday I plan to visit my grandma, who lives a couple of hours away - so I don't get to see her on a daily basis. And for this familial visit, I'm keeping the elephant. They live in cooperative herds led by a matriarch, which sounds like my family and grandma. Elephant families help feed, protect, and even babysit the young, all working together to maintain their close ties.

And what are your weekend plans?

items.title: Your Weekly Meowgazine of 10 Real Feline Rescue Moments That Prove Compassion Has No Pedigree

Grab you feline supurrvisor, scroll down, and meet 10 felines whose lives changed because somebody chose to help.

items.title: A Sprinkle of Sunshine With 22 Cheerful Puppy Memes for Dog Lovers Ready for the Weekend
items.text:
Is there a better way to welcome the weekend than with wagging tails, happy little paws, and puppies who act like every day is the best day of their lives?

Name a better way to start the weekend than with dog memes. If you ask me, spending time with any type of pet is an awesome way to set the weekend mood.

When I lived at home with my parents and got to hang out with my dog every day, we had a Friday-night routine. Right after work, I used to take her on a little walk. Nothing crazy, just a 20-30 minute walk to the nearest park. I always brought snacks, toys, a blanket, and the book I was reading. At the park, I read for a couple of hours while she ran and played with her toy or other dogs. At first, whenever I grabbed her leash, she got very excited and acted surprised. But with time, something crazy began to happen.

My dog is very smart, and she started to understand the pattern: this only happened on Friday afternoons. Somehow, I still don't know how, she understood when to start asking for this walk, and every Friday at 4 PM she would grab her leash and bring it to me, telling me that it was time to get off work and spend time with her. Sometimes she would do it at 1 PM, well before our leaving time, and it was funny to see how time works differently for her. Anyway, that behavior taught me a lot about her and dogs in general.

That excitement she felt is the same as what I feel every Friday. Whenever I turn off my computer and my weekend just starts, it feels wonderful to relax and do the things I've been looking forward to all day. My dog and I share that. If I get off work on time, I go to my parents' house, take her for our weekly tradition, and she still waits for me with her leash.

items.title: Wife torn after veteran husband with PTSD wants to adopt an Akita for safety, but a terrifying run-in with one leaves her afraid of the dog breed
items.text:
It's not easy to both love dogs and simultaneously feel scared of them.

Until I was around 4 or 5, I was totally afraid of dogs. Not as "not liking dogs", but actually terrified. Every time I would see a dog walking towards my general direction in the street, even from very far away, I'd immediately ask my parents to lift me into their arms. Like, crying hysterically for them to do that, even if the dog doesn't even give a shmootz about me. I didn't care - I wanted to be "safe", as far away as possible from the dog. It could be a large dog, just as it could've been a small one, but my kid-self didn't make that distinction. I was afraid, and that's it.

But the thing is, it's not that I disliked dogs, I was just legitimately afraid. For no reason, granted, but I was a very young kid. Today it's not the case - I love all dogs, I think they're pawsome. But I don't have a dog… because I'm married to a woman who is afraid of dogs. She's not the age I was when I used to be afraid of dogs, obviously, but she's still not willing to walk on a sidewalk if she sees a big dog walking towards her. Her story is a bit different and rooted in childhood trauma, but that's a story for another time. And still, the fear is there - so we got a cat (which I adore), but will probably never adopt a dog.

And that's where my issue with the husband in the story below lies. It doesn't matter what the underlying reason for wanting to adopt a dog, or a specific dog breed, because once you have a spouse who is scared - it's off the table. I would never imagine putting my wife in a situation where she's torn over me asking to adopt a scary dog while she's afraid. And I'm sorry, but the fact that the husband here is a veteran with PTSD isn't a reason to adopt a dog his wife is scared of. It's a reason to treat it with therapy, support, and love.

items.title: 21 Cooking Fails and Bad Food for Optimistic Home Chefs Learning to Trust the Process (October 22, 2026)
items.text:
Ever followed a recipe step by step and still ended up with something completely unrecognizable?

That same thing happened to me the other day. I've said here that cooking isn't for me, and I gave it up years ago. But from time to time, I like to see if my cooking skills have somehow arrived, and usually they don't. This last time was no exception. The original plan was to bake a chocolate cake for my best friend's birthday. Simple, right? The worst part is that I've done it before, so I was really confident.

I got all of the ingredients. Mind you, this was not a box cake recipe. This is a chocolate cake very similar to the one from the movie Matilda… very soft and chocolatey. Anyway, it seems simple. Mix eggs, sugar, vanilla, etc. It called for some unusual ingredients, but I added them all and followed the recipe exactly as the TikTok video showed me.

So far, so good. The problem came a few minutes ago, during the first moments of baking. The video said it was important to preheat the oven, so I did; then I lowered the temperature and put the cake in. In that moment, I realized I don't have cooking skills, and probably never will. The cake burned on the outside and was raw on the inside. Completely raw, like a chocolate soup…

items.title: 'Happy Meowloween!': 22 Cats in Halloween Costumes Ready for a Spooktacular Party
items.text:
Who needs scary monsters when you've got your cat dressed as one?

Why do we love dressing up our cats? It's a crazy thing to think about, since most cats don't like being touched or put in clothes. But there's something so cute about it that literally melts everyone's hearts. The most adorable part is that every cat looks so cute and tiny in those little clothes that fit them perfectly. Just look at the pictures I gathered below, and you'll see what I mean; it'll be impossible not to consider dressing your cat in any of these costumes this Halloween.

Cat costumes don't have to be elaborate or complicated. You can put them in a little vinnie, a hat, or some booties, and they'll be ready to go trick-or-treating with you. But it's important that you consider their safety and happiness before your own desires. Because if it were up to us, we'd dress up our pets every day, not just on Halloween, but if you know your feline isn't a fan of clothes and doesn't really like being touched or held… maybe that isn't an option this year. That's a boomer…

The good thing is that, for some reason, there're multiple cats out there that actually enjoy wearing costumes and look happy in the ones they got this year. So, for the rest of us humans who don't own a cat or really don't know any cat who likes to wear clothes, we can have a wonderful time looking at this gallery. I'm already excited to see more ideas like this!

items.title: ‘The Memes Strike Back’: Star Wars memes for Rebels, Imperials and Force Users to Laugh at Across the Galaxy (October 21, 2026)
items.text:
How much money have you spent on Star Wars merchandise? Probably more than you should have…

One would think that being a fan of a franchise only implies watching the movies over and over again and overanalyzing every detail, and while that is a very important part of being a fan, it's not the only thing involved. Nope, being a fan of something, anything, means a whole lot more.

With Star Wars in particular, you have such a big extended universe that you can't just stop at watching the movies and TV shows. No, after a while, the bug of curiosity bites you, and you want to start buying and collecting the graphic novels, action figures, the video games, the LEGO versions of absolutely everything, and the list could go on. If you think we spend enough money on all of that as it is, and you're right, you'd be surprised to hear from people who do cosplay. Yeah, other than having all the collectible items you could think of, cosplayers also pour their heart and soul into their costumes. Which also implies emptying their wallets, of course. That's where all the justifications for all the money spent start: "I deserve it," "I'm treating myself," "This is why I work," and so on…

I, unfortunately, don't have anywhere near as many items as I would like. A few action figures of Luke, Yoda, and Darth Vader, a little LEGO X-wing, one of the original graphic novels, and not much more. Do I wish I had a bigger collection? Absolutely. Can I afford it? Definitely not. I swear, every time LGO puts out a new and improved version of the Millennium Falcon, I want to cry. And you know what else I wish I had? A life-size Stormtrooper suit.

If you've seen at least a few episodes of the show How I Met Your Mother, you probably saw that Barney's character has one of those in his apartment. He's quite a terrible person, but if there's one thing I have always envied him for, it's that stormtrooper. You don't see those everywhere! Granted, my house is relatively small, so it's not like I have much space to put it, but I don't care; I would find a space. Heck, I'd build an entire new room if I had to.

Don't worry, I'm not that insane; I know it would be ridiculous, and I have to get used to the fact that most likely, I will never have one of those. But you know what I do have? A bunch of Star Wars memes!

items.title: 22 Spooky Season Cat Memes for a Purranormal Dose of Feline Fun
items.text:
Trick or treat!

The magic words to get strangers to open their doors to you and give you free candy. Cats trick or treat too, they just don't always tell you they're going out on the town. In honor of Halloween coming in the next few days, here at I Can Has Cheezburger, we're celebrating all month with dressed up, costumed out, cool, spooky kitties who just want some free salmon snacks.

Cats have the most intimate relationship with Halloween, and not just black void cats either! They love the macabre, the spooky, the elaborately dressed essences of what the holiday brings to the table. And what about the coziness? There's nothing a cat loves more than to be snuggled up in soft blankets and covers, fireplace rolling, a Halloween movie on in the background while their pet loving owner cuddles them to kitty dreamland. So if you're a Halloween guy or gal with a feline friend, just know they're celebrating too!

Halloween is my favorite holiday. I know, I know, it's a bit kitschy for fake goths or people still obsessed with Tim Burton films well into their 50s, but who said there's anything wrong with kitsch? Even if you're a 50-year-old whose phone background is Nightmare Before Christmas, it's simply important to celebrate the things that make you feel you. And for a lot of people, it's the whole spooky season, in which Halloween exists in. We're not the only ones enjoying spooky season; there's a whole society of cats celebrating witch hunts, dressing up, and doing seances behind closed doors.

These adorable, yet spooky dressed up cat memes are the purrfect medicine for a bad day, or the inspiration you needed to get into the holiday spirit. There's something ethereal about the autumn and everything it encompasses. The grey skies, the possibility of rain, the brisk air, and the wind pushing stray leaves to and froe. So enjoy scrolling these cats in costume while you prep for Halloween.

items.title: ‘Me and Bro Larping as the Haunted Mattress and Moustache Man’: 17 Absorbent, Yellow, Porous, and Funny SpongeBob SquarePants Memes to Absorb Some Joy
items.text:
Graveyard Shift Episode Memories

This episode is genuinely engraved in my brain. Last night, I was searching for SpongeBob Halloween episodes since I'm a huge SpongeBob fan, and I came across this one that I casually remembered word for word.

Watching it was an incredible experience because, even though I remember what happened and some parts of the script, like the name 'Hash-Slinging Slasher', I hadn't watched it in so many years that it brought back some of those childhood feelings.

It goes like this: Squidward invents a frightening story (yes, always Squidward), and once SpongeBob hears it, every strange invention becomes evidence that the story is real, like it's the details that make it believable. The horror is mostly about how the story is told, more than about what it entails.

Nosferatu's appearance (sorry for the spoiler; it came out like twenty-four years ago) is an indelible memory for me, and I think it's what made me a huge horror fan years later. I believe I understood something about horror when I watched the Graveyard Shift episode: that it's all a matter of perspective.

When Nosferatu appears, everyone acts like he is an endearing character, and suddenly you start seeing this creepy, black-and-white figure with loving eyes. I applied that method to everything that scared me afterwards, and it worked!

I think I just discovered why I could watch so many horror films as a child without being scared. So if you need tips for watching horror films with your friends this spooky season without getting scared, you're welcome. Just think of every ghost or monster as funny or endearing, and you'll be fine.

Also, if you really can't take true Horror, you can watch SpongeBob's Halloween specials, or some other vintage cartoon Halloween special like the one from Hey Arnold! "The Headless Cabbie." Do you remember it? I literally remember it so vividly; there is nothing like a good suspense story. And they're objectively good cartoons, too.

I frequently think about how much SpongeBob impacted my life; I literally think it educated me in so many different ways, lol. I'm like one of those Simpsons fans who can always cite an episode for any given circumstance, but for SpongeBob SquarePants.

I remember his bubbly personality as if he were my friend, and as I got older, I began to understand Squidward (who was just a ridiculous character for me at the time) a lot more. When you're a kid, Squidward is a character that shows you how bitterness and pretentiousness make your life worse, but as you grow up and become more uptight and contemptuous of your life, you identify as Squidward more and more, and watching SpongeBob again can help you remember how silly it is to be living like that.

So I watch SpongeBob SquarePants every so often to remember what life is all about, and I think you should too! At least the Halloween Special, if you're too easily frightened to watch a proper horror film, lol.

items.title: Best friend of the bride wants to back down from the wedding after bridezilla embarrasses her publicly, saying that ‘nobody would ever want to marry someone like her’
items.text:
Have you ever had the kind of so-called friend who needs to embarrass others to make themselves feel superior?

Unfortunately, there are a lot of people like that in the world, and we definitely can't grant them the title of 'friend.' And it's even sadder when those types of friendships happen between women. Seriously, we're already well into the 21st century, and some women are still trying to belittle each other? We are supposed to support one another. We already have enough to deal with in the world to have our own girlfriends trying to tear us down.

Sadly, some people have such low self-esteem that they can't help but embarrass their friends to make themselves look cool in comparison. It's even worse when we're talking about someone who's getting married.

Some brides become bridezillas pretty quickly when they think that, just because it's their wedding day, they can treat everyone like trash. News flash: you can't. They are still your friends and family helping you throughout the entire process, and you can't go around yelling at them, demanding crazy things, or making them feel bad.

I've helped plan my fair share of weddings. All my friends were a little anxious and nervous, but not once did they ever treat me poorly, make evil jokes at my expense, or ask any ridiculous request. They were the epitome of friendship and sisterly love, and they were the most grateful people on the planet toward all the friends who helped them. Which is why, if I had been in this girl's place and one of my friends made those comments about me, I would bail immediately.

items.title: Love At First Bite With These Adorable Little Vampurrs And Their Tiny Fangs
items.text:
Halloween is right around the corner, and while everyone else is busy planning costumes and stocking up on candy, some cats are already dressed for the occasion. They don't need plastic fangs, fake blood, or a dramatic black cape. All they have to do is open their mouths and show off those adorable little vampire teeth.

Cats might spend most of their days sleeping in sunbeams and demanding snacks, but underneath all that fluff are some surprisingly sharp teeth. We're so used to seeing their sweet little faces that it's easy to forget they're technically tiny predators. Of course, it's difficult to take their intimidating hunting instincts seriously when they're chasing a crumpled receipt across the living room.

Some cats have little fangs that poke out even when their mouths are closed, giving them a permanently mischievous expression. Others reveal their impressive chompers during an enormous yawn, looking like they're preparing to audition for the next vampire movie. We have a particular weakness for those tiny bottom teeth that occasionally make an appearance. They're ridiculously cute, especially when paired with a confused expression.

If cats really were vampires, we doubt they'd be particularly successful at keeping their identities secret. They'd spend half the night knocking things off shelves, demanding food, and loudly announcing their presence outside bedroom doors. Forget silently stalking unsuspecting victims. Your average house cat would probably wake the entire neighborhood before managing to sneak up on anyone.

They'd also have some pretty unusual weaknesses. Instead of garlic and sunlight, their greatest enemies might be vacuum cleaners, closed doors, and the terrifying sound of someone opening a cupboard without offering them a snack. We suspect a feather wand would be more effective at distracting a feline Dracula than any traditional vampire-hunting equipment.

Cats already have plenty of experience looking spooky. We've all seen those photographs where their eyes glow in the dark, making them look like mysterious creatures lurking in the shadows. Add a pair of visible fangs, and you've got a perfectly convincing little monster. Never mind that the same terrifying beast probably spent the afternoon sleeping in a laundry basket.

With Halloween approaching, we're celebrating all the fangtastic felines who look ready to star in their own spooky movies. From tiny baby fangs to impressive grown-up chompers, these cats have everything they need to embrace their inner Dracula.

So grab your garlic, keep your neck covered, and prepare to meet some ridiculously adorable little vampires. We can't promise these kitties won't bite, but we suspect they're far more interested in stealing your treats and your favorite spot on the couch.

items.title: 27 Parks and Recreation Memes to Turn Your Inner April into an Andy
items.text:
"Am I interrupting anything important? Impossible. I work for the government."

There are just some days you feel like work is not going the way it's supposed to. You're trying your best, and still, things keep falling apart, or simply not moving forward. Inspiration is not flowing like other days, and energy is running low. That has a scientific name, for those who didn't know. It's called Monday. The legendary weekly challenge to get anything done without an inch of energy left in your body. If only the weekend could have a couple extra days.

That said, if you think Mondays are hard at a regular job, try working for the government. It's like being in the service industry but a lot worse, and with more random people screaming at you for reasons beyond your comprehension.

You could say I am something of an expert in the government-related industries. Not because I have actually worked for the government before, but because I have watched all seasons of Parks and Recreation (more than once, may I add), which basically constitutes an honorary PhD in understanding government functioning. Hey, at least I didn't finish the last season of Grey's Anatomy, because I would be claiming to be a doctor if I had. Thankfully, I chose an amazing sitcom instead.

items.title: Boss continually pings employee during the weekends without offering overtime: 'My weekends feel like they don’t belong to me anymore'
items.text:
When someone is constantly invading your free time, do you have the right to shut them down? What if they're your boss?

Some jobs have a slippery relationship with work-life balance. Some jobs require so much of you and don't respect your boundaries. Some jobs feel like you're making a huge sacrifice to something that you didn't expect to or want to. Other jobs require only what you're willing to put in. But we can all have standards for ourselves when it comes to what we're willing to put up with and not put up with at our jobs. Some bosses act like everything is an emergency, and expect everything to be treated with the same amount of urgency. This doesn't mean that everything is urgent, though. If everything is urgent, then nothing is. Priorities exist for a reason, and it's okay to ask them to be defined for you.

This employee was tired of constantly dealing with work when he wasn't at work. We all need weekends. We all need rest. But that can feel impossible to ask for at work sometimes. Sometimes you might feel pressured to take as little time off as possible. A survey by Solitaired reported that 47% of Americans didn't use all of their PTO in 2024. We're leaving days on the table, as a sacrifice to some greater idea of work-life balance that someone else has put out. It's not a bad thing to rest, and it makes you better at your job if you have time away from it. This employee, though, wasn't getting that from their boss. They wanted to have their cake and eat it too, and the employee was getting really frustrated by it. It's a tough job market, and you likely want to hold onto a position if you can. But at what cost?

items.title: Homeowner moves into new home, realizes neighbor is living in her car on her driveway: 'She parked it at the side furthest from her house'
items.text:
Nobody likes a neighbor who doesn't respect the boundaries of their property, but there aren't many people who can claim that they have actually had them living on it.

There are a lot of people who seem to think that they are entitled to the space that is lived in by another person simply by virtue of being close by. They often believe that this neighbor owes them for one reason or another, or simply hope that they have enough neighborly kindness and generosity that they can continue to exploit it indefinitely, no matter what the repercussions may be for the other individual and their property. They just want to make sure that they are taken care of in a way that they see fit.

Truly, it is a blessing to move somewhere new and have neighbors that are not problematic. It is a privilege that not everybody gets, and at its worst, an intrusive neighbor can really affect somebody's ability to live peacefully in their home. It begins to feel like their house isn't fully theirs because they have to share a part of it with somebody else.

Nobody wants a part-time roommate that they didn't ask for, and what's worse is that they often aren't that easy to get rid of. Once somebody has staked a claim to a piece of yard or driveway, they usually won't back down without a fight. It is a battle that can get pretty ugly if everybody involved really commits to it.

items.title: Person spots a cat wearing a SpaghettiOs can on the way to work and makes a decision that changes their morning
items.text:
You never know what you're going to come across on your way to work. Maybe there's an unexpected traffic jam, a dog wandering around the neighborhood, or, in one person's case, a cat walking across the street with a can of SpaghettiOs stuck on her head. That's certainly one way to make sure someone's morning commute doesn't go according to plan.

Cats have a talent for getting themselves into situations that leave us wondering what on earth they were thinking. They'll squeeze into impossibly small boxes, stick their heads into bags, and investigate just about anything that smells interesting. Unfortunately, their curiosity occasionally gets them into trouble, especially when food containers are involved.

We have no idea how this particular kitty ended up wearing a spaghetti can, but we're glad someone spotted her. The driver stopped to help and managed to remove the can, fully expecting the cat to run away afterward. Instead, she turned out to be an incredibly friendly little lady who seemed perfectly happy to accept some human attention.

Leaving her on the street wasn't an option. The rescuer called their boss to explain that they'd be late to work because they'd found a stray cat. We wonder how often that excuse comes up! We'd certainly have a hard time getting back into our car and continuing to the office after meeting such a sweet kitty.

The cat has since been given the wonderfully appropriate name Sketti Noodle, which might be one of our favorite rescue cat names ever. Considering how she was discovered, we can't imagine calling her anything else.

For now, Sketti Noodle is staying in the rescuer's bathroom, separated from their resident cat. She's already had a bath, and although no fleas were spotted, her temporary caretaker plans to check her more carefully with a flea comb. They've also posted about her in a local lost-and-found pet group in case someone is searching for her.

We're curious whether Sketti Noodle has a family somewhere who would be thrilled to have her home. She's clearly comfortable around people, although that doesn't necessarily mean she isn't a stray. Hopefully, the lost-and-found post helps answer that question.

In the meantime, this little lady has somewhere safe to stay, a human looking out for her, and a name she'll probably never live down.

All it took was one unexpected encounter to turn an ordinary commute into a spaghetti-themed cat rescue.

items.title: Mechanic accidentally installs winter tyres on wrong car, demands customer pay $180 to find and change them: 'I asked why I’m paying them to fix their own mistake'
items.text:
When is it appropriate for a customer to foot the bill for a mistake that wasn't theirs?

While the main objective of any business is ultimately to make money, pursuing a little extra profit at the expense of decency and standards is a surefire way to lose customers who feel like they deserve better treatment when they are already paying for a product or service. Just because a clientele can be difficult or annoying sometimes doesn't mean that the average person just trying to get something done should be treated with contempt.

As in all walks of life, honesty is the best policy if a business happens to mess up whatever it provides to its customers. While there might be some select situations where lies and audacity seem to do the trick, those who care about integrity are better off playing it safe. That is how you have a chance at retaining customer loyalty even if some things go wrong.

Unfortunately, there are plenty of unscrupulous people who do not care about these principles so long as they can make a quick buck. From the perspective of the customer, the best thing that can be done is to call them out and fight for what they are owed. This is not always going to come easily in these kinds of situations. When making money is more important than being fair, a business probably won't go down without a struggle. The question is whether it feels like it is going to be worth the effort.

items.title: Mother-in-law has 1970s crib restored for first grandchild, gets offended when expecting parents won't use it over safety concerns: 'Three generations slept in that crib'
items.text:
Since when has nostalgia triumphed over child safety?

It is not uncommon for families to be big on tradition, whether that comes in the form of a special holiday recipe or maybe a name or heirloom that gets passed down through the generations. In particular, some people get pretty sentimental about the idea of special hand-me-downs that they hope will be used by family members for generations. They see it as a way for relatives to feel closer to one another.

What those who are invested in these traditions often conveniently ignore is that not everybody is going to want to be a part of them. Maybe the heirloom in question isn't their style, or it isn't practical for it to be put to everyday use. Just because grandma lovingly stored away some old thing with the hopes that it would get a second life in the future doesn't mean that this will necessarily become a reality. Being prepared for that disappointment is a part of doing something like this.

Of course, it is almost always important to be polite and show gratitude when a relative has gone to the effort of passing a keepsake down to you. It usually shows that they care; it's just that this care can be misguided occasionally. Ultimately, times change, and what may have been seen as a great investment 50 years ago isn't always going to hold up in the present day. There are more useful ways to provide a gesture of love and support.

items.title: Girlfriend uses his boyfriend's card to order food, even though he told her to delete the card from her phone, she orders $30 worth of food almost every day: 'She’s saying I’m being unreasonable and that I can just pay the minimum payment'
items.text:
To use a card that isn't yours to order food every day when you are fully capable of paying for it, as you have a job, is insanity and particularly mean.

Would you dare to use someone else's card to pay for stuff you want? And would you continue to do so after they have expressly told you not to use it? And, after all that mess, would you disregard the whole thing as a simple thing that doesn't matter, as they can simply pay the minimum balance? I'm 100% sure no one who is in their right mind would do this. It's not only proof that the person is acting completely crazy, but it also shows that the person doing all this is mean. Why mean? Because they are using someone else's hard-earned money to pay for a luxury they don't need. The person who does this is a thief, and I will not change my mind. It is identity theft and the weaponization of someone's money. It is wrong!

I have a feeling that people are afraid to admit when others are mean. Instead of pointing it out or doing something about it, they just pretend everything is fine. When you have a friend who is always making you feel bad, saying things that are supposed to be jokes but are actually disrespectful words, and talking bad about you behind your back. Most people wouldn't say their friend is mean; they would deem them as 'complicated', or they would simply justify their attitude. This is not okay. It's not right that your friend treats you like this. It shows how insecure and jealous they are, but also how mean. But justifying the attitude is no better. You have to speak of things by their true name; it's mean behavior. It's not right to be forgiving of people who aren't looking for forgiveness, and that's exactly what you are doing when you justify these horrible attitudes. Own up to what it is. If they are being mean or disrespectful, do not tolerate it, do not justify it, do not pretend it is fine. Say that is wrong, end the friendship, call them a mean person, do something! To just stay silent is not condemning the actions and let the perpetuate.

So, next time someone treats you wrongly, do something about it. Whether it is a mean friend, a partner that takes advantage of you, or a family member that disrespects you. Stop being passive. Do something about it! Condemn it. In this case, kick her out of your house. She is using your credit card and putting you in debt over food deliveries. I promise you it's not worth it. Get your life in order. To just accept the bad things that people do to you is not okay. Doing something about it is the way to go. Stop letting others treat you badly just because you are too afraid of telling them how you feel; you are better than that.

items.title: 22 Sweet and Romantic Love Memes for Hopeless Romantics Lucky Enough to Find the Love of Their Life
items.text:
Is there anything sweeter than finding someone who makes even the most ordinary day feel like a love story?

I am, without a doubt, the most romantic person I know. And that's saying a lot, considering that I'm surrounded by Libras who live inside a love bubble. I love all things sweet and romantic: movies, chocolates, flowers, cute phrases, random dates, hugs, kisses… my heart starts dancing, and I can't help but put a smile on my face. My boyfriend knows all of this, so he makes sure to be on top of his romance to make me as happy as possible… he's the best; what can I say.

He's my first boyfriend, actually, and how we met is a crazy love story. Want to hear it? Okay….

I was visiting his town for the first time with my best friend and her boyfriend. We decided to go out, so she talked to a friend of hers to come along. He was coming with his girlfriend, and I was going to be the third wheel all night long… sounded terrible. I almost canceled the plan, but my friend told me that they were bringing a guy who wanted to meet me. And guess who that boy was? My current boyfriend. LOL. Isn't that crazy? We met that day, and we haven't been apart since then.

Finding the love of your life is not an easy task. Well, for me it kind of was, but nowadays love isn't something that you find around the corner. People aren't as loving and romantic as before because relationships start depending on social media, technology, likes, and random comments. Please, let's go back in time when things were simpler!

items.title: 23-year-old daughter wants to go on a trip with boyfriend, but her mother forbids her because she still lives at her house, even though she pays rent: ' I told her I wasn’t going to argue and that I was still going'
items.text:
Maybe needing your mother's approval at 23 isn't something a normal adult should have to do. It gives too much control freak.

Being in your twenties but still living with your parents has become more and more common in the last few years. Young adults aren't able to afford to move out, especially if they are studying. That's why relying on family to provide for you is helpful. This doesn't mean that the adult still living with their parents is lazy or childish. Most probably, they do work; they just don't have enough money to fully move out yet. That's why they only give some money to help out. Some have decided on setting some kind of rent in which the adult pays their family the same amount each month. This works as a way to continue to live with your parents but also contribute your part. It's better for them, as it is far less money than a normal apartment would be.

Relying on family to help you out during a financial mishap doesn't mean that you stop being an adult. You are still over 21 and are able to decide what to do, when to do it, and who to do it with. You are an adult no matter where you live. You are capable and in charge of making your own decisions. You are an independent being. If you want to go on a trip, then do so; if you want to work more hours, no one should be stopping you. If you want to move out, you can! You are able to pick an chose what to do; it does not depend on your parents just because they are providing you with a place to sleep. Especially if you are paying them to even live there.

You are an adult capable of making your own decisions, and the fact that a parent thinks they have the right to deny you the ability to do something is hysterical. It is not correct to weaponize someone's living situation to control them. Would they still be acting that same way if it was their parent the one living at their home? I don't think so. If you are over 18, or over 21 if you want to be sure, you are allowed to do as you please. No one is able to limit you, no matter what your financial situation is. Nonetheless, in this particular case, I would suggest moving. You are not getting the respect you deserve as an adult, so it's not convenient to stay there. Moving may not be a clever financial decision, but it is a good one regarding your mental health, which is far more important. Respect is not negotiable, ever. It is something that you deserve, and you give. So the whole existence of a situation like this is unforgivable. You, as a parent, don't have any decision-making power over your functioning adult son's or daughter's life. Learn to deal with it and stop trying to control adults.

items.title: 24 Cute Cat Memes to Make Your Spooky Season Extra Cozy
items.text:
It's finally cold outside. Thank goodness. And that means it's time to cozy up with some cat memes.

Take a deep breath, everyone. Do you smell that? It's the smell of the weather getting colder and pumpkin spice in the air. Spooktober. Meowlloween. Ugh, it's one of our favorite times of the year. Your cat by your side, a blanket thrown over both of you, rain gently tapping your windowsill, a cup of hot cocoa in one hand, and a bunch of wholesome cat memes in the other.
