items.title: 'When You Take a Nap So Good That You Think You Missed the School Bus. But It’s Sunday… And You’re 32': 17 Classical Art Memes That Are Timelessly Funny
items.text:
'Loving paintings doesn't mean loving to paint'. The myth that everybody could benefit from drawing

Ever since I was a kid, I hated drawing. People recommend it to me, even to this day, as if it were a magical tool for stress, or as if everyone reacted the same way to it. It has been very hard for me to get my message across. Drawing and painting don't relax me; on the contrary, they stress me out.

Why do we keep prescribing hobbies to one another? I think this is where humanity goes ridiculous. Everybody seems to accept that people might have different preferences, except when it comes to hobbies. If you dare say you hate painting, people will treat it as a very complex psychological resistance or defense mechanism.

Some hobbies are apparently sacred; it's frowned upon not to like them. The reaction is the same for people who don't like dogs or children. I mean, you're allowed not to like cats or snakes, but if you don't like dogs, you might as well be a criminal.

There is a subtle leap between 'this helps me' and 'this is going to help you'; isn't it obvious? Drawing, to me, is one of those things that is presented as innocent and accessible, when for some people it requires contact with things they despise.

Part of why I hate painting is that you have to get your hands dirty. I use gloves to wash dishes; I wash my hands three times a minute when I'm cooking; it's just not for me. But I would never even think of recommending singing (which I personally love)) to everyone. Some hobbies just have way better PR than others.

Also, we tend to think of artistic appreciation as something that naturally leads to artistic production. I love paintings, art history, museums, films, and sculpture. That doesn't mean I have to become a painter or a filmmaker, guys; lol, I feel like I'm stating the obvious, because I am, but people seem to forget this the moment they want to recommend taking up a hobby.

Some art I just want to appreciate from afar. It's not that I'm lazy; I like playing music, for example. I just don't like painting, people! It feels like I'm coming out of the closet; I'm relieved. I'm going to leave drawing and painting to the geniuses out there.

And when they're done painting, I will use their paintings as really good templates for memes. I don't want you to think I like trivializing art; at the same time, I take it very seriously, and I like to know the historical circumstances of every painting. Memefying it is only a way to further integrate it.

Hasn't somebody said that humour is a vehicle for knowledge? With it, we encode extensive information, and we retain it better. So my theory is that classical art memes help us understand art history. Making them isn't about disrespecting art; it's just another way of producing knowledge.

items.title: 26 Streaming Services Memes to Prepare You For Your Next Subscription
items.text:
Can we rent a DVD for the weekend?

On Friday afternoons, we used to have a little family tradition. My mom would walk with me to the video store, and I was allowed to pick one film on DVD so that we could watch it on the weekend. Sometimes, if I had been extra responsible with house chores and schoolwork, I would even be allowed to rent two films. It was my favourite moment of the week. I would spend hours just trying to decide which film was the perfect watch for the family.

After a few years, renting turned into buying. When my parents decided I was aware enough to start building my own film collection, we did exactly that. Every time we had some extra money, we would visit the nearest DVD store to pick out a film. Little by little, our collection became huge, and it had some of the most beloved cinematographic classics of all time. From iconic productions such as Gone With the Wind, Breakfast at Tiffany's, Singing in the Rain, and Rebel Without a Cause, to hidden jewels like Subway to Paradise, we built a collection that truly felt our own. We could go back to it whenever we felt like having a fun afternoon watch, and it was always quite fun to go through the DVDs one by one, making our choice.

Then came streaming services. Completely changed the game. We stopped collecting DVDs and invested in one account, so we could have access to hundreds of movies at the same time. Little did we know that we were also giving up the idea of actually owning valuable things. There was no more inheriting your collection to your future kids. Despite that, these platforms did open a world of possibility. It felt like there was no TV show or movie you couldn't find, and as long as you had good internet access, there was no place you couldn't get to watching. I went from watching a couple of films a week to watching a couple a day. Being a film lover, I enjoyed that change very much.

items.title: Cat lover who TNRed 20+ stray cats confronted by cat lady for ‘stealing’ her fur babies
items.text:
The subject of what to do with stray cat populations is a contentious one and this story spells out a significant part of the problem surrounding the topic. There are many opinions of what is best to do, but ultimately laws, resources and the luck of having hoomans who are willing to help dictate what happens in reality. Which is how our story begins in a country where TNR is illegal and with a cat lover who took it upon themselves to trap, spay and put more than 20 cats up for adoption. Setting them up in a safe shelter until their furever home comes along. But when this thoughtful hooman was confronted by a local cat lady who was convinced our reducer was 'stealing' her cat children, well, the whole story took a turn for the strange. It turns out this woman had been hoarding these street cats in her home trying to fill the hole left in her heart when her husband had passed.

The woman was understandably attached to the kitties. After all, it is all too well known that when people happen to lose someone they often replace them, or at least attempt to do so with the introduction of a cat child. And while many do so with only one or at most two felines, there are some people with a lack of impulse control and a desperate need for warmth and love who will do things that most of us feline fans feel is unreasonable. The problem is that they do not see this for themselves. They are blinded by the intense urge to fill the void in their souls, their missing piece, and when they get a pawsitive feeling from doing so once, they are often inclined to keep doing it to get that same rush. It is a serious mental health issue and one that ultimately affects the felines for the worse as they deserve the safe, cleanliness and lack of competition that comes with living in a one or at most two cat house hold.

This story truly highlights that in our own minds and worlds as long as we are doing something, we often feel as though we are doing the right thing. But in reality the right thing can be many different things and we remain blinded to the reality of what we are doing. So if you are one of the wonderful people who do whatever they can to help cat kind, just take into account that not everyone is going to agree with your decisions. Not everyone is going to believe that your way is right, and they may be right, they may be wrong. The only responsible thing you can do in the situation is to take accountability for whatever mistakes you make come to light and remember that above all else you are trying to help the cats. The operative word being trying. So try your best and hopefully there is something for you to learn from in this story.

items.title: The Best Batman Memes Making Fun of Release Date Delays and Switching Directors
items.text:
How long is it acceptable to wait for the release of a movie?

In case you have forgotten, which at this point would be expected, the first movie of the new Batman trilogy came out in 2022. That's right, four years ago, and we still don't have a part 2. By the time the actual movie comes out, Robert Pattinson will be old enough to play Alfred instead, and we will have forgotten about the fact that Ben Affleck wasn't the last actor to play Batman.

It's both ridiculous and hilarious. I mean, we know that filming a movie takes time, and it's not just the filming time; it's the post-production, the screening tests, the P.R., and blah blah blah. We get it. Still, this is starting to feel like a bad joke. The last high-grossing film we saw coming out, The Odyssey, only took 91 days to be filmed. And the whole thing lasts three hours. And it has a ton of post-production work. Yet, it didn't take four years to make.

The release date for Batman Part II has been delayed like four times now, and it's natural for us to think that it may never come out. Or it will build tremendous expectations that will be shattered once the movie finally premieres. And now that Matt Reeves is stepping down and Steven Soderbergh is stepping in, we have even more questions.

History keeps repeating itself. Remember the last time something like this happened? Yeah, it was with Zack Snyder and the Justice League movie. He had to step down for personal reasons, and director Joss Whedon took over. He rewrote and reshot more than half of the film, and I'm telling you, the 2017 version and the Snyder Cut are two completely different movies. After that, Snyder could never come back, and the whole trilogy he had planned fell into oblivion.

We're desperately hoping that doesn't happen with this one, especially because the first one was so good! So in the meantime, we're making memes about the whole situation to laugh it off and avoid crying. Let's just hope 2028 is the year for the definitive premiere.

items.title: 'Your friendly neighbor': 25 Spider-Man Memes for True Fans
items.text:
I may not be Spider-Man, but I'm definitely Peter Parker. At least I feel like him.

Spider-Man has always been my favorite superhero, and that is not original on my part. Everyone's favorite superhero is him, unless they are crazy. But why? My first exposure to him was Tobey Maguire's movies that came out in 2002, yes, 24 years ago. As a kid, I was amazed and in love with the whole idea of Peter Parker, a normal boy who happens to get bitten by a spider and transforms into a superhuman with incredible strength and the abilities of a spider. He was so normal in character, yet not physically. The whole concept of him being a smart teen without parents and with a poor background made him more approachable and easier to become everyone's favorite hero. For other fans, the first approach was the comics, in which he showed his witty character and funny comebacks even more. After all, he was just a teen with powers.

The new movies with Tom Holland as the star divided fans at first. Some didn't like the idea of yet another Spider-Man movie with another actor, while others were excited about this superhero entering the Marvel Universe we all know. I was the kind of fan who wasn't sure she was going to like this movie. I was never a full Marvel fan; I just liked the Spider-Man movies. So when it first came out, I completely ignored it. Over the years, I started to watch the whole Marvel universe, and yes, I became a fan. When I got to Spider-Man: Homecoming, I realized they were actually pretty good. That movie that I had been avoiding watching for so long was so much fun. Now I recently watched the last one, Spider-Man: Brand New Day, and that was even better than I could have imagined.

In this last movie, we got to actually see in more deeper length how Peter Parker is. We get to see how he deals with all the problems that being Spider-Man brings to his life: loss, sadness, loneliness, tiredness. It's all too much for a young adult who's just trying to help others and make New York a safer place. We get to fully see the bad side that comes with being everyone's friendly neighbor. This made me remember the comics, where we see his character in a more developed way and the way he deals with the double life. The previous movies seem more comedic; here we see the real deal of the character, and that made him a lot more relatable. Peter Parker can be a superhero, but he is still a young adult trying to do the right thing even when he doesn't know what that is. After this movie, we all got to see that Peter is similar to all of us. He may be incredible, but he's still human. He makes mistakes, he grieves, he suffers. He is just doing the best he can, and who cannot relate to that?

items.title: Man Reflects on Andrej Karpathy's Predictions About How Knowing How to Use AI Will Divide Society:  ‘Give it 5 years. How many of those 80% will still be congratulating themselves for being too wise and righteous to use AI?’
items.text:
This entire AI debate has become a battle over Intellectual Identity and style

The AI vs. SI debate has made us question what it means to be human, to write like a human, or to work as a human. Once bots and agents took over our jobs or significantly changed the way we do them, we started wondering what we bring to the table.

Both being technologically enthusiastic and being skeptical can be ways of oversimplifying the issue. Are we using AI, or using it to prove we're smarter than everyone else? Who is right? People who say we need to learn to work and live with it, or people who say we should focus on making our human capabilities more valuable to stand out in a world full of slop?

I personally think both parties are right, but not in the way you think. We should definitely embrace AI as an assistant at work, except when our job is something that doesn't require AI at all. But I'm also one of those people who think that since AI arrived, human-made stuff has become more valuable, and true creativity has proven itself as un-mimicable by a machine.

AI is known for rapidly changing and evolving, so learning everything about it today wouldn't be a little paradoxical? All of that, in two years, will probably be completely obsolete. We should learn to constantly adapt, stay aware of its advances, and also, why not, of its political implications.

What baffles me is that all the people who discuss the future seem to be too confident about what it will look like, when ten years ago we could've never predicted this SI(AI) revolution.

Artificial Intelligence is definitely changing our thoughts about what it means to be smart, and I like the debates it's sparking. I definitely think the people who think they know exactly how AI works or trust everything it says are the ones in danger.

Perhaps I'm a romantic at heart, but I believe in humanity; I believe in its imperfection and its power to produce knowledge. AI can put together a bunch of words and sound coherent, but it can't think or make new associations; it just works on prompts and preestablished dogmas. I don't think human knowledge can be reduced to logical operations.

We've created language, and language is a beautiful thing. It's plurivalent and polysemic; I'm not sure machines will ever be able to understand that. They can understand formulas and relationships between ones and zeros, but not meanings, feelings, or complex relationships between image and discourse.

And I don't mean we're better than AI because we feel things; I literally mean we can find more meaning in language and make many more associations than a machine. We should use it as a tool, an incredible tool that stores data and can quickly look through it, but nothing more.

While I was writing, I thought about Borges and his story 'The Library of Babel'; I think he might have predicted AI.

items.title: ‘The “Realizing You Aren’t 21 Anymore” Raver’: 13 Ironic Halloween Rave Costumes for Dank and Sarcastic Costume Inspo
items.text:
When your Halloween costume is a meme

We can agree that some Halloween costumes are very niche, and the best of them require a special kind of intelligence to come up with. Ordinary costumes only require you to recognise a character. Ironic, niche costumes are funny because the person who came up with them observed something oddly specific. I call it observational comedy, and I wish I were smart enough to come up with costumes like that.

Some people notice unremarkable things. You have to be very smart to be able to synthesize a very specific observation into a costume, like the energy of someone who works in human resources, the person who goes to a certain kind of party, or the girl who peaked in high school and now looks 68 at 32.

These niche costumes work like inside jokes, and It's funny to try to guess what they are before the person in costume tells you. In the end, Halloween is about being creative and having fun; we can't be dressing like vampires in 2026- archetypes have changed! We can dress as bots now. This Halloween, I'm going to try to make an invisible cultural reference suddenly visible. It's a race to notice the next best thing.

Since when have costumes had to be concrete? Even in ancient Greek theatre, people dressed as concepts. Costume has always been capable of making an abstraction visible. Abstraction in costume, or even in humor, is not an inherently modern thing, or necessarily derived from internet culture. Ancient drama drew on allegory, just like any other art form. Ancient abstract ideas were given names, forms, colors, symbols, just like we do with memes now.

What's mostly changed is the material people derive the concepts from. Rather than personifying Love or Liberty, we represent the overly performative male feminist or the bald Demi Lovato meme.

If you want to go as Dracula, that's up to you, though. Coming up with something original takes a lot of work, and Halloween is also a night to have fun and enjoy, whether you're watching a movie with your friend or at the biggest costume party ever.

It's a night where you're allowed to temporarily stop being yourself. Like at a carnival, anything can happen, and you can explore well beyond the limits of your identity. Every culture has found ways to make festivities around this concept.

Some people confront their fears by ridiculing them with costumes on Halloween, and maybe we can do the same thing with our online anxieties. It's a celebration of disguise and transformation, and we can add our little twist to it.

People have used disguise to make ideas tangible, and we're no different; it's just that our ideas have become more complex. Maybe our most avant-garde costumes will look ancient and innocent to our descendants, and Dracula will be long forgotten by them. It's fun to try to guess what they will dress as. Will their definition of period costume be dressing like us?

items.title: Teh Hisstory of LOLcats: How silly kitties conquered the internet, one cheezburger at a time

items.title: The Best Teacher Memes of the Week (October 16, 2026)
items.text:
There is still more than a month before Thanksgiving break, which means that teachers are going to be pulling their hair out and wishing they chose a different profession until then. Memes are the only cure for that level of stress.

When I was a kid, I liked to think of myself as a good student. I always wanted to please my teachers, and I was never a particularly disruptive kid in class. There were some exceptions to this rule, and I hope all the teachers who are here to enjoy these teacher memes can forgive me for the pain that I've caused to two teachers in particular.

When I was in 8th grade, my friend Brooks and I went into our science teacher's classroom, and put a stink bomb in the trash cans. I have to admit, this was a pretty immature prank for 14-year-olds. That's the kind of prank that you would expect a 3rd grader to pull, but to be fair, when we were in 3rd grade, we didn't have access to a product stinky enough to stink up a whole classroom. The teacher actually evacuated the classroom because she was nervous it was a gas leak. In a way, it was! We never ended up getting caught or getting in trouble for it, which is surprising, because our school definitely had security cameras and they could've checked that we had snuck into the classroom during lunchtime. Maybe our school had faith that we wouldn't do such a childish thing, but they shouldn't have.

The other incident is objectively so much funnier than a stench. One day in 3rd grade, I decided that I didn't want to do the word problems on the bottom on my homework, so I just cut them off with scissors and turned it in. My teacher, Mrs. Williams, confronted me about it, and I lied and said that I didn't know what happened to the bottom half of my paper: it just came that way! It could be easy to judge myself for this, but I never did it again. Even though I didn't formally get in trouble, my teacher calling me out was enough to put away the scissors for good.

items.title: Kitty falls down from the docks, swims struggling to go back to shore, and kind hoomans go out of their way to rescue him and bring it back to firm land
items.text:
Everybody knows that cats don't usually like water, but sometimes they can't get away from it, no matter how hard they try…

We've all seen those videos of dogs in summer, swimming happily in their hooman's pools. They look like they're having the time of their life, and we're rooting for them! But with cats, that is rarely ever the case. There's a reason why most people don't give baths to their cats on a regular basis, and that's mainly because they don't react well. The cat can end up getting stressed out, and we can get a few bites and scratches as our war scars.

This doesn't necessarily mean that all cats hate water, or that you'll never be able to give your furbaby a bath even if they come home completely dirty. It just means that we need to be more careful with the way we approach the whole cat-water issue, since some of them might be scared of what water means.

I've mentioned before that my cat is a rescue, and the first time they brought her home, she was covered in dirt from head to toe. She needed to get a bath, since she couldn't be in the house all dirty. At first we thought she was just a grey cat, but after the bath, we found out that she was actually black and white! A bath was definitely necessary after all. That first time, she reacted well. She seemed to be too scared to try to do anything, but now, I can't be sure how she would react. Mind you, she's getting dangerously close to needing another bath. She spends a lot of time running around and hiding behind and under furniture, so yes, she comes out all covered in dust quite often, and although I get her clean as best as I can, I might find myself in need of scheduling another bath soon.

In this case, it wasn't that the cat was escaping from bath time; nope: the poor thing fell out of the docks and into the sea, and was desperately trying to swim back to shore.

items.title: 'I love you more': 20 relationship memes to send your long-distance partner
items.text:
Do you miss your partner and need to reach out to them now without sounding too clingy? Send them a cute meme!

My love language? Sending memes. You don't need to constantly be over-explaining your feelings. Saying everything that goes through your mind just so someone can understand the deepest feelings you have inside may be a little much. Not saying that you have to be repressed. But as someone who has heard full-on declarations about how others feel about me and what crosses through their minds when they see me, it is a bit uncomfortable to know that much. You can just say that I'm important to you, and that would most likely be of better effect to me than the whole speech you prepared, but that doesn't mean that is the same way for everyone. Maybe I'm a bit avoidant, and my experience doesn't represent every couple; some people do love to hear everything that their loved ones feel for them, as that is the only way they can actually believe it. But some of us get uncomfortable and start feeling the need to run.

Love language is very different for each person. Some people love physical touch, being held, hugged, kissed, while others prefer to be told that they are loved. Words of reassurance are great for them. Some couples like to show their love with material things, gifts that were thought through and match the person they are given to, while others would just prefer to spend time together. Even if it's in silence, the simple act of enjoying each other's company is more than enough. This can vary, and sometimes in a couple, one may like one kind of love language that the other person despises. That's why it's important to make an effort to make the other feel loved the way they like while still keeping your own boundaries. For example, I'm not a fan of words of affirmation; they completely overwhelm me. Most times, a simple phrase like 'I love you' is fine, but a full-on confession is definitely too much, at least for me. I prefer spending time together, even if we are only watching TikToks each on our own phone. It makes me feel calm that I can share the space while we each do what we like.

These differences may be hard at first for a new relationship. It may seem like a rock on the road when you don't agree on the love language you both prefer. But there is nothing wrong with that. You can like different things. As I said, I do not particularly like the whole words of affirmation thing, but when your partner does, you make an extra effort to make them know they are important to you. You start saying all the things that you would not like to hear, but they do. You love them in the language they want, so they can feel your love for them even more. The effort that you make is valuable, is a representation of love, and is another love language on its own.

items.title: The 22 Best Penguin Memes of The Week
items.text:
Penguins, penguins, and more penguins.

Do you ever get so stressed about your job or your studies that you wish you could just be a penguin deep diving into the ocean with your friends? I sure have. But I never actually met a penguin; I'm not sure I know enough about them or what they usually do. Maybe they also go through stress over other things. Maybe they aren't just the relaxed little animals that we all believe they are. Maybe they also get so overwhelmed by something or need a mental health day once in a while. Maybe they also go to sleep wishing the days had more hours, or that the holidays were closer. I don't know much about them, but it is fun to imagine that their lives aren't that different from ours. But most probably they are.

One of the first encounters, to some, the only one, most people have with these little animals is through TV shows and movies. By this I don't mean documentaries or science shows. I mean those animated media that we are exposed to since kids. Looking at these images of penguins made me think about all the famous penguin characters that grew up with us over the decades. The first one that comes to mind is the ones from the movie Madagascar. Those 4 witty penguins are most of our first encounter with the animal, and we end up loving them. They are funny with a bit of maleficence inside them, a perfect combination. They became so popular that they even got their own TV series, Penguins of Madagascar. Another example of a first encounter with these animals is definitely the characters from Happy Feet.

One TV show that is incredibly popular and also features a penguin as the star of it is Pingu. I never thought that the series was that popular and known by everyone. I always thought it was a bit niche. But no, it has an enormous fandom that is always creating new memes and reviving scenes from the show. For the ones that have not watched the show, it is about the adventures of a penguin called Pingu and his family, who live in an igloo in Antarctica. It's a show animated in stop motion with six seasons that was on air from 1980 till 2006.

Incredibly, a lot of us have never actually seen a penguin in real life, as we haven't visited a place cold enough for them to live. But we do know about them and love them. And for that, we need to thank TV shows and movies. They were our introduction to these cute little animals and the reason we know about them. Yes, of course we learned about them in school, but we love them as much as we do thanks to the visibility they got from the media. Let's hope we get even more shows and films so they become as popular for the new generations as they were for us.

items.title: 'Of course I know that book, it has been on my TBR list for 3 years': 22 Readers Core Memes
items.text:
Do you like entering bookstores 'just to see what they have', only to end up buying the whole store and having no money left? Then these memes are definitely made for you.

Books are a necessity. I stand by that. People not only need to read to make their brains function, but they also need to experience literature for its own sake. Readers and non-readers need to discover and enjoy the art behind the books, the story behind the words. Reading isn't only a hobby you do on the beach while on vacation. It is an activity that should be part of most of your life. You, as a human being, need to get involved with a book, either learn from it, open your horizons, or at least enjoy a good read.

I hate the people who say they don't need to read; that they can just watch the movie. That is not the same thing at all. You are talking about two different art forms that have nothing to do with each other. They can have the same story as the basis of it, but they are definitely not the same. One gets you interpolated into a new world by the words. The author thought through before writing every single word, having in mind a place and people that you are only capable of imagining through the words they chose to make you imagine it. A film has a bigger team behind it that makes sure that your vision and the director's are almost the same. The character will be portrayed exactly how the director wanted, not like your brain imagines through a list of characterizations that were spread in little details throughout the whole book. You can definitely enjoy the movie adaptation of a book more than the book itself, but that doesn't mean that one is the other. They are still two different and independent forms of art. As I said, an opposite experience.

Reading a book is such a great activity, but I get the fact that not everyone sees the fun in it. For those people for whom the idea of picking up a book and reading it seems impossible, I have some advice. If you say you don't like any book at all, then you are doing it all wrong. You aren't going to enjoy every single boook your read, but you will at least enjoy one. You just need to find the genre that you like, an author whose writing skills you like reading. This can only be found by trying books; reviews may be helpful as a way to shorten the list of to be read books, but to fully know, you will just need to sit and read. So good luck on that challenge, and please give a chance to that book you bought years ago, expecting one day to have the time to read it. Start tonight, read 30 minutes, and see what happens. I promise you, when the right book enters your life, it changes it forever.

items.title: 'This looks so magical': Twitter debates and shares their thoughts about the freshly released trailer for the new Chronicles of Narnia movie
items.text:
Here we have yet another remake/adaptation to add to the endless list!

Don't get me wrong, I'm really excited about this movie, especially because it takes me back to my childhood and the memory of watching the Disney version of The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe, which, in my opinion, is one of the best fantasy movies ever made. It was a shame the saga was left unfinished, especially because the first movie was amazing and a fan favourite to this day. I haven't talked to a single millennial/older Gen Z who hasn't seen and loved Narnia. And I believe that's part of the problem.

The first movie did great. It had a pretty big budget, and it collected a good deal of money after coming out, so they gave the green light to the second movie, Prince Caspian (which is my personal favourite, and it makes me cry every time I watch it), but this one wasn't as successful as the first. And basically no one saw the third one. The first is the one that is remembered and talked about the most, both when it first came out and now, 20 years since it premiered.

Netflix and Greta Gerwig seem to think that this world still has a lot to give, and I agree, which is why I was so excited when the project was first announced. They already planned to adapt all the books, a very ambitious plan if you ask me, but hey, they've got the budget and the will to do it. I love the fact that they are adapting this in chronological order, something that hadn't been possible to do so far, but I still have my reservations about the vision they have for this world.

You'll see, the trailer looks amazing, that's for sure, but it also looks like every other movie that has come out in the last five years. The whole Narnia universe has a very specific tone: magical, mysterious, with an underlying sensation of imminent danger. It's an uncanny feeling, and it doesn't look like they're adhering to it. Let's remember, these are all kids facing forces that are way bigger and more powerful than they are, both in The Magician's Nephew and in the story of the Pevensie siblings, so the stakes are always high, always on the verge of collapsing, with the weight of the world placed on the shoulders of a bunch of 14-year-olds.

Now, in case you were wondering, yes, I did read The Magician's Nephew when I was younger, so I can give you my honest opinion about this. And in my head, the story looked vastly different from what it's presented in the trailer. The issue with book adaptations is that they hardly ever look exactly the way we saw them in our heads while reading, since the movies are not our own creation, but someone else's imagination. Still, many aspects and details can coincide, since it's the same story. Well, I don't feel that way about this trailer. If someone had played it without telling me what it was, I wouldn't have known.

However, it's yet too soon to give a well-informed opinion, since the movie won't come out for a few more months. We'll have to wait and see the complete product before we can properly discuss it. In the meantime, you can browse through this list of comments that were made on Twitter. Some people are fascinated; some others are appalled. You can share your own thoughts with us on the matter.

items.title: Morris the tiny cat finds his biggest bestie in Champy the horse, and 14 years later, they're still proving the sweetest friendships can come in the most unlikely sizes
items.text:
Adorable animal friendships come in all kinds of shapes, sizes and species.

And no, this is not something that we are saying as people who have seen a picture on the internet at some point. We have evidence. We have authority on the matter. We, the ICHC editors, have been writing stories about animals for years, and we have seen some of the cutest and strangest animal friendships over our time here. As just the tip of the iceberg, a few of our personal favorites include: the cat who became friends with a rescued giant lynx, and don't worry, the itty bitty feline is the one putting the big one in his place, not the other way around. The orange cat who adopted a baby bunny that lost its mother and is now basically raising that bunny as her child. And the cat who became best friends with a bearded dragon. Literally chilling together in the same tank, yes.

After all this time, we wanted to believe that no interspecies animal friendship would surprise us. We know that these friendships come in all kinds of shapes, sizes and species. And yet, even I, someone who has spent over 6 years writing content about cats, was surprised by this one. Because this is not just a cat and a horse being friends. It's not just their difference in size and in ways of showing affection. It's the time that they have been friends.

Morris was adopted in 2013, and although at first, the idea of being friends with a horse was strange to Morris, eventually, Champy won him over. And they are still friends right now. That's nearly 14 whole years of love.

items.title: Girl has a date with a guy, but at the last minute, he changes plans and invites her to his cousin's engagement party with his whole family, she doubted but finally went: 'His grandma asked when we were getting married'
items.text:
You can't just change the date at the last minute.

First dates can be the best or the worst time of your life. A lot of expectations and doubts occur about a first date. We don't know a lot of things: like who is paying, if it will be split, or whether they are going to dress accordingly, if they will be funny or annoying, serious or somber. We think we know who we are meeting as we have been texting beforehand, but we really don't. This is a stranger with whom we happened to hit it off over text. But it can all go downhill no matter how much chemistry you had over text. It can easily be the best person to message but the worst to keep a live conversation going. Or the other way around, they can be a little dry through text but extremely nice and upbeat in real life. It all depends on the person you are having this date with; in the end, that is the only thing that matters.

I haven't been to a ton of first dates, but I've had enough to know the signs that will tell me whether that person is a keep or if I should run. I never had an awful first date; at least nobody asked me to go to a family gathering on the first date. But I did have some really good ones. I'm not an expert of any kind, but I do have expectations when I go out with someone for the first time. Firstly, I like to go to a public place; a cafe would be the best place as the music is nice and low for maintaining a conversation but not too intimate to make things uncomfortable. Secondly, I won't go out with someone whom I haven't texted first; I need to get a grip on your personality first. It doesn't matter if I already know them in person; I need to know how good of a texter they are. And thirdly, if you say one thing that makes me uncomfortable during the date, then I'm a goner. I will not stay seated if I'm having a bad time; I will pay for my things and leave instantly. If I wanted to be in a bad place, I would go to a horror movie, not spend an afternoon with a stranger.

These are my rules for first dates, but I know for a fact that they don't matter when you meet the right person —except for the last one; that one is always a must-follow. Every person is unique, and they have their own rules about them. The most important thing is to hit it off with the other person and enjoy a nice time together. In the end, when you meet the last person, that first date will probably be amazing no matter what that first date looks like. It can be a date at a 5-star restaurant and be awful, or the best one: a simple picnic in the park.

items.title: ‘The Memes Strike Back’: Star Wars memes for Rebels, Imperials and Force Users to Laugh at Across the Galaxy (October 14, 2026)
items.text:
Disney is developing a new Star Wars video game, and we're just sitting here, hoping they honor the franchise and don't fall into the dark side…

After the failure of some of their last few productions, one would think that Disney would try to let the franchise alone for a while, or at least try to improve the quality of its next productions a little bit more. It's not like they have issues with money. After all, it is a well-established franchise owned by a multimillion-dollar company. The problem here is that they keep stripping the heart away from it and treating it like a never-ending money grab. They could easily put in more effort on the scripts and the plots. It's almost like they keep going just on vibes and completely disregard the foundations of the original movies. Everything could have been easily fixed, had they hired writers who actually cared about the franchise, their characters, and the world they were getting into. That's the key part: it looks like they don't really care. They are just making everything look rambunctious and over the top, but without real substance. Well, their strategy doesn't seem to be working as well as they think, because half of the fandom is disappointed, and the other half doesn't even bother to watch most of the recent movies, TV shows (I admit I am one of them), and video games. And on that topic, they are developing a new video game along with Epic Games, the company that created Fortnite.

That would be all well and good, save for the fact that they are developing it using almost exclusively artificial intelligence to write the code. As if they had not sucked the life out of the franchise long enough, here they come and use the one thing that is the absolute opposite of human. I understand that artificial intelligence can be a useful tool sometimes, and it makes everything go faster. But please, could someone just do something manually? Not all the time, just once in a while, to remember what it looks like when actual humans sit down and exercise their craft. If we get distracted for a second, they might just start making entire films that way and only using the actors' faces. Well, that might be an exaggeration, but you get my point. My money is on the chances that this video game won't be anywhere near as good as Jedi: Fallen Order, Star Wars Battlefront, or even the LEGO Star Wars.

I love this world very much, and it's disappointing to see how they keep downgrading it. I would love to go back for a while to the original canon, the one with the comics and all the adventures our favourite characters had after taking down the Empire. The one that explained the golden age of the Jedi and their temple, the different meanings of all the different lightsaber colors, and basically, all that now is a part of Star Wars Legends. So, I have a proposition for you right now: let's forget for a while about this debacle and go back to enjoying and being happy with the original Expanded Universe while we experience some galactic laughs with this set of memes.

items.title: New research finds pawsitive connection between higher cat populations with happier humans, and we're feline pretty good about it
items.text:
Usually, bold statements made on social media are just there to make you click with no follow-through, but I actually went and read the study so you don't have to. Spoiler alert - it's a bit more complicated than "more cats = more happiness," but it does tell us something us feline fanatics have known for a while: cats help reduce feelings of loneliness and help foster emeowtional connections!

"Countries with more cats tend to have happier populations" is a statement I would love to advertise everywhere. In fact, let's turn it into a bumper sticker so all the cat moms and dads can have something to be proud of. It makes sense, if you think about it: cats are great pets for both introverts and extroverts, they fill normally empty houses with love and give their hoomans a reason to be excited about when waking up and coming home from work. But, like all things on the internet, it's not quite as simple as X + Y = Z.

I came across this bold statement on @sociaty's post while scrolling and, knowing how cool this could be to share on I Can Has Cheezburger, I decided to dive in and actually check to see what this study said. I read through the whole thing, all 14 pages of it. Here's what they actually studied : the researchers wanted to see if a country's happiness could be connected to factors beyond traditional measurements such as wealth, income, and healthcare. For this study specifically, they wanted to check if countries with more cats were happier, and if a purrticular parasite connected to cats was connected to lower happiness.

In short, yes, they did find a pawsitive correlation between more cats and greater happiness. However, they still found that wealth matters significantly (duh) and that more cats didn't necessarily mean more exposure to the parasite.

Cats are great pets, we don't need a scientific study to prove that. They teach us about boundaries, empathy, the power of choosing the purrson you love, and companionship. Regardless of how they affect a country's happiness, we know that on an individual level, they make our days better and our lives more interesting. Even if they do add 300% more chaos to our day-to-day lives.

items.title: Cat escapes his home, insteantly regrets it, and attempts to break back into the house in the silliest way: 'The risk I took was calculated, but man, am I bad at math'
items.text:
All cats seem to desire to see the outside world, but not all cats know what to do with the world once they have seen it.

This is something that I know from purrsonal experience. Cats have an unyielding fascination with the outside world. Yes, all cats. Not every cat tries to escape the house. Not every cat tries to become a hallway kitty at every opportunity. Cough, talking about you, Mia. That's my cat, if you didn't know yet. But all cats sit in front of the window for hours at a time. Maybe some of them like it for the birdwatching, while others like looking at the rain. Maybe some of them are fascinated with the sounds, while others are with the lights or the other people or animals outside. But they all do it. Because they are all fascinated.

And yet, these same cats are also spoiled as heck. We know it, but they… don't. They have no idea what the world outside is actually like. They don't understand that it is not full of free food and fluffy blankets. Our houses are all they know, and our houses have all of these things. The cat in today's story proves exactly this. His attempted escape, for once, was successful. But before his pawrents could start worrying about him being gone, before they even noticed he was gone, they found him again. Attempting to break into the same house that he escaped from. And as is the job of the internet, the first thing that people did when they saw this now iconic image is meme the heck out of it.

items.title: ‘I honestly don't get why corporate work is often treated as uniquely awful compared to every other form of labor’: Employee reflects on whether we’ve exaggerated how bad corporate jobs are
items.text:
It's not that corporate workers are exaggerating; it's that we have several conflicting ways to measure suffering

Why is sitting in an office sipping your favourite coffee, answering emails, and filling endless Excel sheets while alienated from the product of your work considered the epitome of modern work-related suffering, while other types of (very demanding) labor are considered 'just regular jobs'? Are we treating some kinds of suffering as more 'prestigious' than others?

We all have a clear image of what a corporate job looks like, even if we never had one. The fluorescent lights, the endless lines of cubicles and desks, the greyish carpets, and the millions of people working hours on end on something they'll likely never see come to fruition.

For us, the corporate employee became the symbol of someone who sold their life to a company. This might be because an existential crisis is much easier to narrate when everything else seems fine: no obvious physical costs to our job, it looks comfortable, and it's financially stable. When we're still unhappy in a situation like that, it forces us to look underneath the surface.

This is where I think we go wrong. People actively participating in anti-corporate discourse online have had terrible experiences of alienation working in those companies, and they tend to idealize whatever lies outside of them.

It's very easy to quit and dedicate your life to ceramics when you have huge savings from years of financial stability and disposable income. Probably, someone who has worked selling ceramics from the start is having a much rougher time.

I think we have fallen into the trap of who gets to dominate a narrative online, a terrain that exponentially benefits those who can articulate their suffering in language that best fits the medium. We're simply not listening to those who are tired of making physical effort for way less money and are accumulating debt and stress, because they're not talking about their suffering on Reddit with words that resemble French existentialism.

White-collar workers are often depicted as people who betrayed themselves: they were creative before, and they 'sold their soul', but why don't we make the same association when we think about a construction worker? We tend to naturalize that type of labor and see those people as having way less potential to begin with.

There is a peculiar kind of doom corporate workers feel when they cannot really justify their work as useful. It's much easier to say 'I'm a gardener' or 'I'm a lawyer'. We can easily picture what that person spends their time doing, and what they produce. In corporate jobs, people can spend endless hours doing something that doesn't produce a specific product.

What does a 'Project Manager' actually do? Is it a real skill, or can anyone do it? Can they see what they've done at the end of the day? Or are they just a minimal fraction of a gigantic enterprise that could easily replace them with anyone else? If corporate jobs disappear, could those workers contribute to the world with any skill?

items.title: 35 Dungeons & Dragons Memes for Weary Adventurers Looking for a Long Rest
items.text:
At this point in the timeline of real-life historical events, all I want is to gather with my friends to escape the magnitude of real life and collectively imagine fictional historical events we create ourselves.

If that's not the meaning of D&D, I don't know what is. Like, yes, I think D&D is really cool, but after the last few years, I feel like it leveled up and acquired a new feat called "self-inflicted historical events." This would probably be the description: "When you add this feat, you provide a better imaginary dreamscape to the people who play you, giving them the chance to experience imaginary historical events their characters cause themselves, given they have reached a high enough level. If your Charisma is 16 and above, they will also enjoy it."

Yes, this was me trying to imagine a feat given to D&D itself. It's all imagination, as D&D players we can do whatever we want. I'm just tired of having to go through real-life history - it just keeps on happening, and there's nothing any of us can do to stop it. I just want to go back to the days when we all sat around a table, rolled some dice, and there was literally nothing else to worry about. But those days are over - we're adults, doing adult things, worrying about adult worries, and setting schedule conflicts (you know exactly what I mean by that).

So in difficult times like these, I take up the mantle and make it happen myself. I'm brewing a D&D campaign as we speak because three of my friends wanted to play. One of them brought in another friend of his, and there's me - the humble DM. I'm writing a homebrew campaign where they'll start as shady workers for a low-tier mafioso (inspired by the beginning of the Second Darkness adventure path), sent by him on a mission to steal important and remote treasure, only to betray them and lock them in (inspired by Bartrand Tethras from Dragon Age 2), flying away on the back of the hideous dragon that guarded that treasure (inspired by the last Harry Potter book), only to then discover they have awakened an ancient locked-up god the dragon used to serve (loosely inspired by Rovagug of Pathfinder).

I can't wait to make them chart the course of history in our collective imagination!

items.title: A Fresh Batch of Feline Tweets Sweeter Than a Cup of Apple Cider (October 12, 2026)
items.text:
When you need a little Monday morning pick-me-up, viral online cat content is here to the rescue.

Every Monday morning, week by week, we find ourselves in crisis. The weekend is never long enough. We're tired. We don't want to start another work week. And to make things worse, as if on purpose, our cats are always cuddlier on Monday mornings. Ehem, I'm talking about you, Mia. That's my cat, for those of you who didn't know. And although she liked to cuddle and take up half the bed every night, on Monday mornings, she always cuddles up to me the closest.

Or maybe it's just my imagination. Maybe I just prefer staying at home and cuddling with a cat. But I can't. I have a duty. To Mia - to make money and get her the fanciest weight management food there is. And to all of you guys - to entertain, to make your Monday mornings a little bit easier. And for cat people like us, the best way to do it is just to bring you more pawsome cat content. And as I do every single Monday, I have put together the best, most viral cat Tweets of the previous week. Drink your coffee, catch up on the cat news of the online world, and start your day on the right paw. Sometimes, it really can be that simple.

items.title: 30 Feline Funnies for People Sepnding a Sweet Sunday With Their Cat
items.text:
Every week, I'm excited to reach Sunday and just rest with my cat - it's the highlight of the week.

There's nothing like reaching the weekend and knowing the burden of the workweek is behind you. That's how I feel. I actually love my job, because I deal with cats all day (duh), but there's nothing like the feeling of knowing I'm going to have an entire weekend of cat time. And I'm sure every cat pawrent out there shares this sentiment with me. But when the weekend starts, we all still have things to do - everything we didn't have time to do during the week. Whether it's that extra laundry load, dealing with a pile of dishes, cleaning around the house, etc. And even if it has nothing to do with chores at all - like time spent with friends and family. They all happen on the weekend, but… then comes Sunday, and you can finally chill with your cat.

Sunday is all about my cat lying on my stomach while I'm in bed, and she purrs like a tiny tractor in the field. Sunday is all about my cat walking with me in the kitchen, trying to trip me between my legs, until I reach her treat drawer and give her an extra one. Sunday is all about having bursts of energy for playtime with my cat, making her zoom around the apartment like a tiny rocket made of fun and meowgic. Sunday is all about my cat, and that's the most beautiful thing in my week.

If you're a cat pawrent who waits for Sundays just like me, I have the thing for you - some great feline funnies. On Sundays, I love taking my cat's nap breaks as time to relax before the upcoming Monday - and of course, I do it with even more cats online. I don't want to bother her during her sacred cat nap. And I bring you some feline funnies to do just the same - I'm inviting you to have the best Sunday you can with your cat, and some internet cats as well.

items.title: Friend brings their girl cat over despite warning that this owner's boy cat is a bit of a flirt, and he immediately proves his owner right, pulling out all the purrsuasive moves
items.text:
All cats are special in their own silly ways.

I admit, before adopting my cat, Mia, I didn't know anything about cats. I thought I did. I've always loved looking at cat things on the internet and attempting to pet stray cats outside. But I didn't know what it meant to have a cat, no really. And I didn't know how much I didn't know. She trusted me, though. She adopted me, knowing that I am more than willing to learn everything that I need to. And I did. I learned how to spot when she's not feeling well, I learned how to play with her, I learned what her different meows mean - everything. But of all the things that I learned, the one thing that surprised me the most is figuring out just how much personality cats have. And in my time on the internet and writing for ICHC, I have learned another thing: all cats have personalities, but orange cats have purrsonalities.

Orange cats are unique. They are special. They all share one brain cell. Just one. Between all of them. Every once in a while, one of them will have a turn with the brain cell and shock us all with their intelligence and cunning. The rest of the time… they are just orange. And we could not love them more for it.

We've seen orange cats with all kinds of quirks. There's an orange cat who is obsessed with snap peas. There's another orange cat who likes going number 1 in the sink just "to feel included". There's one who gets ready with his owner - every single morning without fail. And that is just the tip of the ice berg. And still, even after everything that we have seen, this viral pair of orange cats still surprised us. We have never seen a cat flirt before today. And now that we have, all we can is… of course he's orange.

items.title: Wildlife Photographers Capture Big Cats in Boxes Having Their Cutest “If I Fits, I Sits” Itty Bitty Kitty Moments
items.text:
Everyone knows that all cats, in their hearts, are just itty bitty kitties.

Look, we have been cat people on the internet for a long time. Even before starting to write about cats for a living, all of us writers were into cats and cat memes and cute pictures of cats. Back then, it was just a hobby. Now, six years later, I'm a purrfessional. I know my way around cats. And I also know that I might have lost my mind ever so slightly throughout the past six years. Because my confidence when it comes to cats applies… to all cats. This is my confession. Don't tell my loved ones. I, deep in my heart, truly believe that - if given the chance - I could become best friends with a big cat.

Of course, I haven't lost my mind entirely. I understand the risks, I do. And I haven't tried to befriend one.. yet. But I also know this fact: all big cats are just like house cats. It's enough to watch one video about big cats or spend just a few minutes looking at big cats in zoos, and anyone would see it. Big cats stretch like house cats. They roll around onto their backs and show their bellies like house cats. They clean themselves, they scratch their ears, they sneeze - all just like house cats. And you know what? The reason I might try to befriend them is not even all of that. It's the fact that big cats are goofy like house cats too. items.title: Hilarious Cat Memes Capturing the Never-Ending Battle Against Feline Fur
items.text:
You're dressed, you're ready to leave, and then you look down. Cat hair. All over the shirt you could've sworn was clean five minutes ago. Out comes the lint roller for what has to be the third time today.

Cat owners spend a lot of time removing fur from things, only for it to immediately come back. We vacuum the couch and the cat takes a nap on it. We wash our sheets and they jump onto the bed. We fold a pile of clean laundry and suddenly that's the best sleeping spot in the entire house. Sometimes it feels like they're watching us clean and waiting for their chance to undo it.

Black clothes are especially risky if you have a light-colored cat. One cuddle before leaving the house and everyone you see that day gets to know you have a pet. We've definitely been out somewhere, looked down at our clothes, and started picking off hairs one by one. At a certain point, you just have to decide which ones are worth removing.

Then shedding season hits and things get even hairier. You brush your cat and pull out a clump of fur. Then another. Then another. You look at the growing pile, look back at the cat, and wonder how they still have so much left.

That is, if brushing is even allowed. Plenty of cats love it, but plenty of others would rather keep every loose hair attached to their body until they're ready to deposit it directly onto your pillow.

After enough time with cats, you start building fur removal into your routine. There's a lint roller near the door. Maybe another one in a bag. The vacuum gets a workout. You learn not to leave clean clothes sitting somewhere accessible unless you're willing to wash them again.

None of this stops us from making the problem worse. The cat walks over while we're wearing a clean shirt, and we're still picking them up. They climb into bed, and we're still letting them under the covers. They settle onto our lap, and we're definitely not moving them just to protect our pants.

So the fur stays. On the couch, on our clothes, in our bags, and probably on whatever we're wearing right now.

We can lint roll later. The cat wants cuddles.

items.title: Koko the gorilla adopted two kittens, but their bond became something much bigger than an adorable animal friendship
items.text:
Did you know that on her birthday one year, Koko the gorilla asked her handlers for kittens? Koko fell in love with one, and the other fell in love with her. Their bond would later teach us a lot about how animals purrceive the world.

There are certain things that cat people don't need fancy scientists to tell us. I know my cats have favorite people (sometimes I'm one of them, other times, unfortunately not), I know they hold grudges, and I know that they can somehow detect the exact meowment I'm about to stand up and choose that moment to fall asleep on my lap. This was one of my first cues to truly understand that animals have their own inner lives, but because I'm a cat owner, my "Aha!" moment just happened to be through emotional manipulation.

Koko the gorilla gave the rest of the world a pretty compelling reason to wonder about animals' consciousness as well. In 2015, when Koko was 44 years old, two tiny kittens named Ms. Gray and Ms. Black entered her life. According to the Gorilla Foundation, Koko was gifted a litter of kittens for her birthday on July 4th. She fell in love with Ms. Gray, and Ms. Black fell in love with her.

She watched them, nurtured them, protected them, and even developed individual relationships with them as they grew. She would sign "cat" and "babies" when referring to them, she wanted to be around them constantly, and honestly, I can 100% relate to that. I can not only relate to that, I do that every day.

Koko's love affair with the feline species wasn't new, either. Decades before, she famously bonded with a kitten named "All Ball," a relationship that put the unlikely animal pair on the cover of National Geographic! Unfurtunately, All Ball passed away later in life, and Koko's caregivers described her behavior in one simple way: mourning.

We can sit here all day and debate exactly what Koko understood. Even after decades of research, scientists still debate interpretations of her signing. But we don't need Koko to have been secretly composing Shakespeare in gorilla sign language for her relationship with those kittens to matter. You can see it in the video below.

There she was, a walking powerhouse of a mammal, adjusting herself around kittens small enough to fit in the palm of her hand. She sought out their comfort. And their kisses, cuddles, happiness, and attention.

That's exactly what loving a cat looks like. Learning your tiny little weirdo's quirks and habits, discovering which scratch means "Moar scritches!" and which means "you have exactly 3 seconds to remove your hand before the claws come out." Missing them when they're gone. Rearranging our lives around their comfort without entirely understanding why we're doing it.

Maybe consciousness isn't about whether another creature can explain its feelings to us, but we see hints of it in whom they choose to sit beside, whom they search for when they're gone, and whom they learn to hold gently. For us cat people, that idea is purrfectly understandable - we've been getting emotionally attached to tiny, fuzzy weirdos who can't speak our language for thousands of years.

Koko just happened to be one of us.

items.title: The Sims Memes for The Obsessed Gamers Who Will Soon Loose Their Sight for All That Playing
items.text:
If you weren't obsessed with The Sims growing up, did you even have a childhood?

Being a teenager with a laptop in my lap, lying in bed, playing The Sims until my thighs burned from the computer overheating was the best part of my teen years. That is everything I wanted to do. And, no surprise at all, I still love doing that. Sometimes we associate games, or even the idea of gaming, with something only kids and teenagers do, but that doesn't have to be true. Adults, and even elders, are allowed to spend their free time playing games on computers or consoles; it isn't just designed for kids. Everyone is allowed to play, and there is a game for everyone.

When I was younger, I played on the PlayStation 2 all day; I loved it. Always buying new games to try out. My mom was always looking at me weirdly when I played. She didn't understand what I saw on that console that she wasn't able to see. To her, it was just a dumb game with animations that weren't even that good; to me, it was the best way to spend the whole summer. One day she asked to play with me. Beforehand, she was never interested, so when she asked, I was thrilled. At first, she still couldn't understand it; everything seemed too boring to her. One day, we found the perfect game, Guitar Hero, one of the best games to ever exist. She had so much fun, and she finally understood why I liked playing so much.

For my mom, that was the game that made her understand, but for so many others, The Sims were the reason why they even spent money on their first computer. It's a game that will make almost anyone interested in it. You can build, you can play, you can create a whole new world. What is better than that? So if you still don't feel very sure about computer games, I insist that you try out The Sims; it may be the reason why you finally understand why everyone else is obsessed with games.

items.title: Why do cat people accept behaviors that would seem bizarre to anyone else? — Cat pawrents share the strange feline habits that unite the community: 'My cat will only drink water out of a red solo cup'

You might be surprised at your capacity to live with things you once thought you couldn't handle before.

One of our most defining characteristics as hoomans is our adaptability. We learn quickly and can adapt to not only new environments, but also new mental states and new problems relatively quickly compared to other species. We wanted to learn how to get things from point A to point B faster? We invented the wheel. Floods destroyed our crops? We learned how to build canals and aqueducts to channel water to places we wanted it to be. The hooman history of tool building and adaptation is actually pretty neat when you start to look at it from this purrspective.

But now? We have all the comforts we could ask for. Homes with climate control, running water, and cars that take us efficiently and safely from point A to B with incredible speed, so what did we do? We searched for the next big challenge - living with cats.

Truth be told, hoomans have been cohabiting with cats for a long time. And in the thousands of years since the first cat domesticated itself, I'm pretty sure not much has changed. We tell the cats what we want, they ignore us, and then they do whatever they want and we have to live with it. Sound furmiliar? It definitely does to me. I've been trying to teach my cats that the kitchen counter is forbidden for close to 10 years.

Cat owners may not gather together a lot like dog owners, but we do have some common expurriences that connect us together - the main one is learning to live with your cat's weirdo quirks. Some cats are obsessed with chewing on plastic, some dunk their toys in water and then demand you take them out, and others come up with things not even our wildest imaginations could think of. We all were purrplexed by them at the beginning and by now, we accept them as part of our daily routines. They may make our lives a little more complicated, but in the end, our felines accept us with all of our flaws, faults, and habits, so why shouldn't we accept them with theirs?

items.title: 20 Hocus Pocus Memes To Get Your Heart Conjure by This Witches Once Again
